item.title: Dylan Harper expects to start season with hot hand
item.description: San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper works on his jumper at practice at Madison Square Garden in New York, Wednesday, June 10, 2026, ahead of Game 4 of the NBA Finals against the New York Knicks. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'll enter the nationally televised opener against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Tuesday night "very confident" in his outside shot after hitting a team-high 57.1% from 3-point range on 3.5 attempts in the preseason. The Spurs host the Blazers in a rematch of the 2026 Western Conference finals, won by the Spurs in seven games, at 8:30 p.m. at the Frost Bank Center. "I've worked at it all summer, so there's no reason for me to be hesitant," Harper said of his perimeter shooting. "No reason to pull back. Biggest thing is just taking the right shots at the right time." The 20-year-old second-year pro drafted No. 2 overall in 2025 led the Spurs in preseason scoring with a 14.8 average after tallying 19 points against the Sacramento Kings on 7 of 12 from the field (3 of 6 from distance) in a 126-97 victory on Friday in the preseason finale. Last season, he hit 34.3% from downtown on 2.6 attempts on his way to averaging 11.8 points. "Through the year last year, (his outside shot) was incrementally improving, and he's a ridiculously talented young player who has really matured and really started to build a foundation of habits," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. With the Spurs starting a speedy, downhill three-guard lineup of Harper, De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle to go along with Devin Vassell and Victor Wembanyama, the team needs Harper to shoot well from deep to help spread the floor. "I think shooting from the perimeter was a big thing for me" to work on in the offseason, Harper said. "And I think just getting more comfortable with my shot, get more comfortable shooting off the dribble, and just try to be as efficient as I can." item.title: Nahida Akter replaces Nigar Sultana as Bangladesh's new T20I captain, Sobhana Mostary named deputy
item.description: Nahida Akter has been appointed Bangladesh's new T20I captain, with the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) confirming the decision to Cricbuzz on Sunday. Nahida succeeds Nigar Sultana, who stepped down from the role following the Asian Games to focus on her game. Sobhana Mostary has been named vice-captain of the side. Nahida Akter Takes Over T20I Leadership “We sat with members of the selection panel along with others and decided to hand over the T20I captaincy to Nahida. Sobhana Mostary will be her deputy,” Rafiqul told Cricbuzz on Sunday. The board believes Nahida's experience in the leadership group makes her the right choice to lead the T20I team. The left-arm spinner had served as Bangladesh's vice-captain since Sultana was appointed captain in 2022. “Nahida has been the vice-captain for a pretty long time and now we feel the time is right to give her the responsibility of our T20I squad,” Rafiqul added. Nigar Sultana to Continue as Bangladesh's ODI Captain Sultana's decision to relinquish the T20I captaincy will not affect her role in the 50-over format. The wicketkeeper-batter will continue to lead Bangladesh in ODIs, having captained the team during their recent three-match tour of Australia. The BCB was reportedly caught off guard by Sultana's decision. It is understood that the former T20I captain was disappointed with the way she had been treated by the board in recent times, prompting her to step away from the leadership role in the shortest format. Bangladesh's Next Assignment Bangladesh's next assignment will be the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy in Thailand, where their campaign is scheduled to begin against Pakistan on November 12. The tournament will provide Nahida with an early opportunity to establish herself as captain and guide the team in her new role.

item.title: Patriots vs. Jets live updates: Score, news, discussion for NFL Week 6
item.description: Coming off their most dominant win of the season, the New England Patriots (3-2) are now looking to extend their win streak to three. Standing between them and that goal is a familiar opponent: the New York Jets (2-3), who themselves are entering Week 6 off a victory. From that perspective, the setup seems perfect for a highly-contested game. That said, the Patriots are clear favorites at home: not only have they looked like one of the best teams in the NFL the last two weeks, they also have gotten some significant reinforcements lately. Wide receiver A.J. Brown is back off injured reserve, while cornerback Christian Gonzalez is making his comeback from a two-game absence. Add the fact that left tackle Will Campbell and running back TreVeyon Henderson have both been cleared for the contest as well, and you can see why the home team earning a third straight W is the projected outcome. Will the Patriots indeed be able to do so, however? Let’s find out together. Welcome to our Patriots-Jets live tracker and community discussion. Live score: Patriots 0 : 3 Jets Sunday, Oct. 18, 1 p.m. ET | Gillette Stadium (Foxborough, MA) | Broadcast information | Game day roster | Inactives | Weather forecast First Quarter Winning the coin toss, the Patriots started the game on defense — and slowly. The unit gave up first-down pass plays to tight ends Mason Taylor and wide receiver Garrett Wilson before some runs by Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis brought the Jets into the New England red zone. The drive eventually stalled, but the visitors still took a 3-0 lead on a 42-yard field goal. | Patriots 0 : 3 Jets A.J. Brown was part of the Patriots’ offensive starting lineup, and the target of Drake Maye’s first pass attempt. However, the throw was batted at the line of scrimmage to end the team’s first possession in a three-and-out fashion. Patriots fans, join the game-day huddle! item.title: UH football game at Utah to be featured on ESPN's College GameDay
item.description: Houston Cougars quarterback Conner Weigman, left, celebrates with wide receiver Koby Young after connecting for a 48-yard touchdown catch during a NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) ESPN's College GameDay is making the short drive down Interstate 15. After spending this weekend in Provo, Utah, for BYU-Notre Dame, ESPN's popular pregame show will set up Saturday in Salt Lake City in advance of the top-20 showdown between Houston and Utah. It will be the first time the Cougars' game will be the featured matchup on GameDay since 2011 against SMU. Houston's game vs. Utah will kick off at 9:15 pm. on ESPN. The GameDay show starts at 8 a.m. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Giants-Saints, Week 6: Live updates, discussion, score, highlights
item.description: New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston drops back to pass. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Follow and discuss all of the action right here as the New York Giants try to win a fourth straight home game when they face the New Orleans Saints at MetLife Stadium. Game time is 1 p.m. ET on FOX. In-game updates First quarter TOUCHDOWN GIANTS – Jameis Winston finds Tyrone Tracy as a check-down, and Tracy does the rest. The Giants lead the Saints 7-0 after the extra point from Dominic Zvada. TRACE LEAPS IN FOR SIX 🫡 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/46WyC4t2iK — New York Giants (@Giants) October 18, 2026 Tyrone Tracy Jr. makes a defender miss on a third-down reception for the TD. Good job by Jameis Winston to get the ball out under pressure. Giants 7, Saints 0 — Jordan Raanan (@JordanRaanan) October 18, 2026 Another big reception by Isaiah Likely followed by a Tyrone Tracy run in Saints’ territory. Jameis Winston delivers a 24-yard strike to Isaiah Likely. Really nice throw into a window as Malik Nabers cleared that area out. Giants into the red zone on next play on a Tyrone Tracy Jr. run — Pat Leonard (@PLeonardNYDN) October 18, 2026 The Giants convert 4th and 1 with an interesting take on the Tush Push. 3rd and Likely. First down, Winston to his tight end — Pat Leonard (@PLeonardNYDN) October 18, 2026 The Giants bring pressure on 3rd & 6 and Tae Banks did well to stick close with Chris Olave and force punt. The Tae Banks redemption arc is still ascending! pic.twitter.com/tNQyi6LQ6z — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 18, 2026 The Giants’ defense brings the pressure and gets off the field, forcing the punt after the Saints pick up a first down. Nice play by Deonte Banks on Chris Olave, who basically is injured #Saints entire offense. — Ryan Dunleavy (@rydunleavy) October 18, 2026 The Giants can’t take advantage of their field position as a pair of screens go backward and Jameis Winston misses Isaiah Likely on the third and long. The Giants start with fantastic field position after the Saints’ kicker misses the landing zone. The Giants will get the ball to start the game after the Saints win the coin toss and defer to the second half. Pre-game updates Some thoughts before the game gets underway. The Giants are 3-1-1. The Saints are 1-4. Despite that, FanDuel Sportsbook lists the Giants as 1.5-point underdogs. The Giants are coming off a 27-27 tie last week against the Washington Commanders. They are 2-0-1 with Jameis Winston starting at quarterback following the Jaxson Dart injury. The Saints have lost three straight. Their only victory of the season was a Week 2 24-17 overtime win over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2. See our comprehensive Giants-Saints StoryStream for all of our week-long coverage leading up to the game. item.title: FG disagrees with W/Bank over H1 124% debt servicing/revenue ratio
item.description: Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government has disagreed with the World Bank on the latter’s debt servicing/revenue ratio for the first half of 2026, put at 124 percent. The bank in its recent Nigeria Development Update (NDU) reported that federal government debt servicing was 124 percent above its revenue. However, the Federal Ministry of Finance, in a statement, yesterday, faulted the bank’s analysis, explaining that the debt servicing figure included those of the state governments and that it was, therefore, wrong to analyse it against the federal government revenue for the period under consideration. The statement read in part, “This conclusion is misleading, for three reasons, the government said. “The interest figure includes debt the Federal Government services on behalf of other tiers of government, including external loans to states. “Measuring this against federal revenue alone overstates the ratio which is only meaningful when debt and revenue cover the same level of government. “The reported revenue is also incomplete. It excludes independent revenue already earned by government agencies and enterprises but not yet remitted to the Treasury. ” In addition, more revenue is typically earned in the second half of the year than in the first due to the statutory timing of certain tax payments. This is why the ratio stood at 156% in H1 2025, while the full-year 2025 debt-service-to-revenue ratio was below 60%, down from 97% before the reforms. ” This is a clear sign of the progress delivered by the current administration’s reforms. “Between the first half of 2025 and the first half of 2026, federal revenue rose by 72%, from ₦3.6 trillion to ₦6.2 trillion. Interest payments rose by a much slower 38%, from ₦5.6 trillion to ₦7.7 trillion. ” Revenue is therefore growing almost twice as fast as interest costs. As a result, the interest-to-revenue ratio fell by 32 percentage points in a single year, from 156% to 124%, and the gap between interest and revenue narrowed from ₦2.0 trillion to ₦1.5 trillion. This is the result of reforms working, not a sign of fiscal distress. “Debt sustainability is assessed on a full-year basis, not over six months. The same World Bank report projects Nigeria’s full-year 2026 debt service, covering both interest and principal, at 46% of revenue. “This is the appropriate benchmark, and a guide to avoid the invalid conclusions being drawn. “Every naira borrowed by the Federal Government falls within the limits approved by the National Assembly under the 2026 Appropriation Act and the approved borrowing plan. “All borrowing is conducted in full compliance with the Fiscal Responsibility Act 2007 and the Debt Management Office (Establishment) Act 2003, and is published regularly by the Debt Management Office. “The Ministry welcomes informed scrutiny of public finances. item.title: ACC Power Rankings: Wake Forest, SMU, and North Carolina Impress in Week 7
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS - OCTOBER 17: Miami defensive back Bryce Fitzgerald (3) intercepts an FSU pass to the end zone in overtime to end the game (also pictured, defensive back Dylan Day (23), defensive back Damari Brown (2), defensive back Omar Thornton (0); Florida State wide receiver Micahi Danzy (8), wide receiver Jayvan Boggs (15)) the Miami Hurricanes faced the Florida State Seminoles on October 17, 2026, at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Samuel Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images UNC at Duke, Florida State at Miami, and Pitt at Boston College gave the ACC some interesting battles this weekend all of which led to major changes in this week’s ACC Power Rankings. As always, be sure to check out the accompanying video and support us by supporting our sponsor, Section 103. Discount code below! 17. Syracuse (Prev 15): Syracuse slowed down Louisville’s excellent duo of running backs named Brown, but Lincoln Keinholtz ran for 53 yards and 2 rushing TDs to go with his 310 passing yards and 1 passing TD. They forced two interceptions which kept things close. It was 28-23 late in the third quarter when the Orange got their second INT of the game. They failed to capitalize and exchanged punts several more times. In the 4th quarter, they got to the Louisville 11-yard line with a first down but settled for a field goal to make it 28-26. Louisville would get another touchdown to push the lead to 8 (after a missed PAT) and Syracuse couldn’t score again. 16. Georgia Tech (Prev 14): An interception and lost fumble got the battle of the Techs off to a bad start for GT. They trailed the Hokies 24-3 at halftime. The Yellow Jackets began the second half with a 42-yard TD run and a 37-yard TD pass which turned a blowout into a battle. It wasn’t enough for them to dig out of the hole though, and they lost 34-24 to the Hokies. GT is now 2-4. 15. Stanford (Prev 17): Stanford handled their business with a 34-7 win over Elon. They are now 3-4 with wins over Hawaii, Georgia Tech, and Elon. Their four losses have been by an average margin of 43. In a way, they’re like Clemson except instead of those blowouts only coming to Miami and an excellent non-conference opponent (LSU for Clemson, Notre Dame for Stanford), the Cardinal have also been blown away by Wake Forest and Duke. They get NC State on Friday at 10:30 p.m. in another event made for TV but terrible for actual fans. Perhaps that advantage can help them make further progress in these rankings. (Photo by Samuel Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images UNC at Duke, Florida State at Miami, and Pitt at Boston College gave the ACC some interesting battles this weekend all of which led to major changes in this week’s ACC Power Rankings. As always, be sure to check out the accompanying video and support us by supporting our sponsor, Section 103. Discount code below! 17. Syracuse (Prev 15): Syracuse slowed down Louisville’s excellent duo of running backs named Brown, but Lincoln Keinholtz ran for 53 yards and 2 rushing TDs to go with his 310 passing yards and 1 passing TD. They forced two interceptions which kept things close. It was 28-23 late in the third quarter when the Orange got their second INT of the game. They failed to capitalize and exchanged punts several more times. In the 4th quarter, they got to the Louisville 11-yard line with a first down but settled for a field goal to make it 28-26. Louisville would get another touchdown to push the lead to 8 (after a missed PAT) and Syracuse couldn’t score again. 16. Georgia Tech (Prev 14): An interception and lost fumble got the battle of the Techs off to a bad start for GT. They trailed the Hokies 24-3 at halftime. The Yellow Jackets began the second half with a 42-yard TD run and a 37-yard TD pass which turned a blowout into a battle. It wasn’t enough for them to dig out of the hole though, and they lost 34-24 to the Hokies. GT is now 2-4. 15. Stanford (Prev 17): Stanford handled their business with a 34-7 win over Elon. They are now 3-4 with wins over Hawaii, Georgia Tech, and Elon. Their four losses have been by an average margin of 43. In a way, they’re like Clemson except instead of those blowouts only coming to Miami and an excellent non-conference opponent (LSU for Clemson, Notre Dame for Stanford), the Cardinal have also been blown away by Wake Forest and Duke. They get NC State on Friday at 10:30 p.m. in another event made for TV but terrible for actual fans. Perhaps that advantage can help them make further progress in these rankings. Do you want to support STS writers? You can do so by supporting our sponsor, Section 103. They deep dive school traditions to create thoughtful designs artfully applied to insanely comfortable tees, polos, hats, and more. Be sure to use our promo code STS10 so you get 10% off your first order and we get credit for sending you their way. Their founder, Steven, has been good to us and we think you’ll love their Clemson, Virginia, Virginia Tech, and Georgia Tech merch. Click here to explore. 14. Pittsburgh (Prev 8): Last year, Syracuse beat Clemson in Death Valley, but lost QB Steve Angeli to an Achilles injury. The Orange went on a long losing streak after that and the win at Death Valley ended up being the lone bright spot of their season. A similar story may be shaping up in Pittsburgh. After going to Blacksburg and earning a thrilling win over Virginia Tech, but losing Mason Heintschel in the process, they’ve now dropped consecutive games to UNC and Boston College. 13. Boston College (Prev 16): QB Mason McKenzie threw for 295 yards while the defense held Pitt to just 21 points. The Panthers were on to their third QB option, and Corey Dailey finished just 11-of-25 with two INTs. The Eagles couldn’t run the ball but recovered a fumble and generally forced field goals to knock off the reeling Panthers 27-21. 12. California (Prev 13): The Bears hosted Wake Forest and were non-competitive. They started Jackson Brousseau over Jaron Keaewe-Sagapolutele at QB. Brousseau was very good in their win against Virginia Tech last week but couldn’t engineer a scoring drive in the first half against Wake and they trailed 34-0 at halftime. JKS entered in the second half and got them a single touchdown in a 41-7 loss. The Bears fired Justin Wilcox for always having Cal be a fringe bowl team and now they are worse. Cal is 3-4 and their win over Virginia Tech last week feels awfully surprising. 11. NC State (Prev 12): The Wolfpack licked their wounds from last week’s blowout to Wake Forest. Up next is the dreaded 10:30pm Friday ACC game at Stanford. 10. Virginia (Prev 11): Virginia is starting to look a lot like Clemson, but with a worse defense. Beau Pribula and his receivers are not effective through the air, straining the run game, and putting a lot of pressure on the defense. SMU was favored to win this matchup in Dallas well before the season, but Virginia’s offense looking this punchless feels disappointing, nonetheless. SMU beat Virginia 23-13 with Kevin Jennings throwing for 246 and 2 TDs while Beau Pribula had just 137 and 0 TDs. 9. Duke (Prev 4): North Carolina held Nate Sheppard to 77 yards on 20 carries (3.9 YPC) but he still had 11 receptions for 98 yards and a receiving TD. Sheppard may be the offensive MVP in the ACC if you exclude QBs. He is outstanding and had 175 of UNC’s 373 total yards. Duke fell behind 17-0, stormed back to take a 20-17 lead, and then surrendered the game-winning TD to the rival Tar Heels to lose at home to UNC 24-20. 8. Florida State (Prev 10): Florida State may be the best 3-4 team in decades. They outplayed Miami for much of the game, but Malachi Toney came up with too many big plays down the stretch to push the game into overtime. The star receiver THREW for a 2-point conversion in the second OT to give Miami an 8-point lead. An unfortunate, non-obvious holding penalty erased an FSU TD that would have given them a chance to force triple OT with a two-point conversion of their own. QB Ashton Daniels was excellent. He threw for 3 TDs and ran for another while accumulating 329 total yards. He was a low-cost transfer portal add that everyone including me scoffed at. He has been really impressive. They get an open date before hosting Clemson. We’ll see if they’re heartbroken and quit after the rivalry loss or if they’ve proven they can compete with the best and rally from here. Norvell’s hot seat watch will be fascinating. 7. Virginia Tech (Prev 9): Ethan Grunkemeyer has been a very solid starting QB for the Hokies. No, the Hokies aren’t ready to compete for the 12-team playoff ( maybe not if the upcoming 24-teamer was starting in 2026 — which you can hear about here ), but this has been an impressive, rapid turnaround under Coach Franklin. They go to Clemson next week in a game that will draw storylines and serve as a de facto ACC Championship elimination game. VT appears to have the advantage at QB, but Clemson holds the advantage in the secondary. Grunkemeyer vs. the Clemson defensive backs will be fun. 6. North Carolina (Prev 7): Is North Carolina good? They’re at least competent. After nearly beating Clemson, they went to Pittsburgh and earned what will officially count as a ranked win (although Pitt is bad without Heintschel). Now, they’ve coupled that with an impressive road win at Duke. WR Jordan Shipp had 75 receiving yards and a TD. TE Jelani Thurman added 52 and is one of the best TEs in the conference. They’re not flashy or dominant, but they’re highly competent and on the rise under Bill Belichick. If they up the talent level again next season, they may be a real pest. 5. Louisville (Prev 6): We expected things to look better for the Cardinals, but despite this being closer than anticipated, they won at Syracuse. They’re 4-3 and only the NC State loss is really head-scratching. Wake Forest — their other ACC loss — has proven to be very good. item.title: Caleb Williams does something only 2 NFL MVPs have ever done
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears warms up prior to the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Huntington Bank Field on October 18, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images A few weeks ago, Pro Football Talk dug up an interesting statistical nugget about Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams and his chance to do what only Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes have done: throw 50 career regular-season touchdown passes with 15 or fewer career interceptions. We can now check another accomplishment off the list for Williams in his young career. His Week 2 hamstring injury slowed his chase for this milestone, but he got that 50th touchdown pass today on their first drive against the Atlanta Falcons on a 14-yard strike to Colston Loveland. Caleb Williams' first drive back ends in a TD to Colston Loveland 🐻 CHIvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/krhXYNpu6F — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 Caleb now has 5o touchdown passes to 14 interceptions in 37 career regular-season games. Mahomes is a six-time Pro Bowler with 2 NFL Most Valuable Player awards and three Super Bowl rings, and Jackson has 4 Pro Bowls and two League MVP awards, so Caleb is in good company with his latest milestone. item.title: NFL puts out statement on Week 7 Saints-Steelers game in Paris amid mass protests
item.description: NFL puts out statement on Week 7 Saints-Steelers game in Paris amid mass protests appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NFL has confirmed that the New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers will play their Week 7 matchup in Paris as scheduled, despite escalating protests across France. The league’s decision comes amid growing security concerns ahead of its first regular-season game in the country. The historic matchup is scheduled for Sunday, October 25, at Stade de France, with kickoff at 9:30 a.m. ET. According to Front Office Sports, the NFL issued a statement Sunday addressing preparations and security arrangements. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters,” the league said. The NFL added that both teams are receiving regular updates and that league sites have experienced no disruptions. The statement followed another weekend of widespread demonstrations across France. Approximately 550,000 people participated in Saturday’s protest, according to the BBC. Authorities also made at least 1,200 arrests amid escalating violence. Demonstrators have raised concerns about rising living costs and proposed education spending cuts. Videos from Paris showed police deploying tear gas and water cannons as confrontations intensified. Despite those developments, the NFL has not announced any changes to the game or its surrounding events. The matchup represents another milestone in the league’s international expansion, with Paris joining its growing list of regular-season destinations. It will also mark the sixth of nine international games scheduled for the 2026 season. For the Saints and Steelers, preparations remain unchanged as both organizations await further security updates. The NFL’s position remains clear: Sunday’s game is proceeding as planned, although officials continue monitoring conditions in France. Related: 3 players Commanders must target at 2026 NFL trade deadline Related: 49ers’ perfect Jauan Jennings trade offer to Vikings to get reunion at NFL trade deadline

item.title: Why Marvin Harrison Jr.'s Texans debut was bigger than the stats
item.description: It will be some time before the Houston Texans and their fans can assess whether the team's recent trade for wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. will be worth the hefty price. But no one is going to grumble about MHJ's debut. The Texans defeated their AFC South rivals, the division-leading Jacksonville Jaguars , 34-31 on Sunday, Oct. 18, when Ka'imi Fairbairn drilled a game-winning, 49-yard field goal as time expired to avert overtime. Harrison didn't have a major statistical impact on the game, catching three passes for 34 yards. But, with just a few practices under his belt, he was a significant component of a Houston pass game that carried the offense against a stout Jags defense. “Marvin Harrison Jr. – they brought him in, he had no really time to practice, and he did exactly what they needed him to do,” said former former Pro Bowl defensive tackle Gerald McCoy, now an NFL Network analyst, said on “GameDay Final.” Harrison's three catches matched his season high with the Arizona Cardinals, and his 34 yards represented his second-best output of the season in that department. “He had three first-down catches today," McCoy said. "He’s a big-bodied receiver, and they needed him to go in, catch the ball, help us move the chains, and they did that today. I’m excited to see what this team has moving forward, because that defense will be better. If the offense is rolling like this, everybody look out for the Texans.” All the NFL news on and off the field. Sign up for USA TODAY's 4th and Monday newsletter . This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Why Marvin Harrison Jr.'s Texans debut was bigger than the stats

item.title: Atiku tackles Tinubu over Police Exit Bill
item.description: …says serving officers dip into pensions By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to explain his delay in acting on the Police Exit Bill, alleging that serving police officers are dipping into their pension savings to feed their families while retired personnel struggle to survive on meagre stipends. Atiku said the plight of serving and retired officers demanded urgent action on police welfare, including a salary review and resolution of the pension concerns raised by retirees, following the pay increase approved for members of the Armed Forces. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, on October 18, Atiku recounted cases of retired officers allegedly living on inadequate pensions, searching for menial jobs and begging for alms after decades of service. “Men and women who answered Nigeria’s call for decades are now waiting outside its legislature for Nigeria to answer theirs. Bola Tinubu should be ashamed that it has come to this,” he said. Atiku cited the case of a retired Assistant Superintendent of Police who allegedly receives a monthly pension of ₦29,000 and told him that more than 120 members of his association had died in the past three years. He also recounted how a retired Assistant Commissioner of Police allegedly resorted to begging at the Central Mosque in Abuja after failing to find work. “No former officer should have to be discovered in distress before Nigeria remembers what it owes her,” Atiku said. In another account, he said a retired officer in Bauchi had resorted to gathering firewood for sale to afford food, while some serving policemen had allegedly withdrawn 25 per cent of their pension savings to meet their families’ needs. “We ask them to risk their lives for Nigeria while they wonder how to feed their families and whether their country will stand by them when their service ends. That is a disgrace,” he said. Turning to the Police Exit Bill, Atiku said the legislation was sent to Tinubu in March but that the President had yet to make his position known as of October. Citing Section 58 of the Constitution, he said the President had a 30-day period to signify assent or withhold it from a bill presented for assent, and demanded an explanation for the delay. “Bola, a bill gathering dust cannot buy food or medicine. Tell Nigerians what you have done with it,” he said. Atiku urged the National Assembly to publish the bill’s formal status, demand an explanation for the delay and determine the constitutional steps available to resolve the matter. He also pledged that, if elected president in 2027, he would introduce a Police Dignity Guarantee Plan to settle verified pension arrears and gratuity claims, establish a pension floor, provide healthcare coverage for serving and retired officers, and ensure timely support for families of personnel killed in service. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, on October 18, Atiku recounted cases of retired officers allegedly living on inadequate pensions, searching for menial jobs and begging for alms after decades of service. “Men and women who answered Nigeria’s call for decades are now waiting outside its legislature for Nigeria to answer theirs. Bola Tinubu should be ashamed that it has come to this,” he said. Atiku cited the case of a retired Assistant Superintendent of Police who allegedly receives a monthly pension of ₦29,000 and told him that more than 120 members of his association had died in the past three years. He also recounted how a retired Assistant Commissioner of Police allegedly resorted to begging at the Central Mosque in Abuja after failing to find work. “No former officer should have to be discovered in distress before Nigeria remembers what it owes her,” Atiku said. In another account, he said a retired officer in Bauchi had resorted to gathering firewood for sale to afford food, while some serving policemen had allegedly withdrawn 25 per cent of their pension savings to meet their families’ needs. “We ask them to risk their lives for Nigeria while they wonder how to feed their families and whether their country will stand by them when their service ends. That is a disgrace,” he said. Turning to the Police Exit Bill, Atiku said the legislation was sent to Tinubu in March but that the President had yet to make his position known as of October. Citing Section 58 of the Constitution, he said the President had a 30-day period to signify assent or withhold it from a bill presented for assent, and demanded an explanation for the delay. “Bola, a bill gathering dust cannot buy food or medicine. Tell Nigerians what you have done with it,” he said. Atiku urged the National Assembly to publish the bill’s formal status, demand an explanation for the delay and determine the constitutional steps available to resolve the matter. He also pledged that, if elected president in 2027, he would introduce a Police Dignity Guarantee Plan to settle verified pension arrears and gratuity claims, establish a pension floor, provide healthcare coverage for serving and retired officers, and ensure timely support for families of personnel killed in service. The proposed plan, he said, would also include a police salary review, clearer records of pension contributions and entitlements, and published payment schedules to improve accountability. “We will provide for the Guarantee in the budget and publish what has been paid,” he said. The post Atiku tackles Tinubu over Police Exit Bill appeared first on Vanguard News .

The QB also has several years of connection with Darius Cooper, so hopefully Cooper continues his impressive streak on Sunday. Join Bleeding Green Nation on game day! Stay on top of every Eagles update and debate every snap with other diehard Birds fans. The past two weeks have been really wild for Eagles fans, and the uncertainty seems to grow by the day. The GM still has just under a month until the NFL trade deadline, but if the team puts together a decent performance this week and can just hold strong while they get injured guys back, there’s still a lot of reasons to believe in the roster. item.title: Position Grades: Michigan
item.description: ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 17: Andrew Rappleyea #87 of the Penn State Nittany Lions runs for yardage against Zeke Berry #10 of the Michigan Wolverines during the first half of a college football game at Michigan Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Aaron J. Thornton/Getty Images) | Getty Images So, I guess that was fun for a half, no? Not really? Oh well, let’s just go ahead and get this over with… Quarterback: F Rocco Becht almost single-handedly lost Penn State the game with his three turnovers, all of which led to Michigan cashing in for touchdowns. That’s your difference-maker, right there. Running Back: C- Carson Hansen had a TD run in what was otherwise another unremarkable game on the ground from the running backs, as PSU rushed for a total of 65 yards on 30 carries for a whopping 2.2 rushing yards. Wide Receiver: B+ Chase Sowell has been the lone Iowa State transfer who has actually turned out to be worth the hype at this point. Sowell had a whopping 11 catches for 151 yards and a TD, and probably would’ve had more if he had a better QB throwing him the ball. Brett Eskildsen also caught three balls for 29 yards. Tight End: C+ The tight ends in total, caught 12 balls for 78 yards as PSU, with Andrew Rappleyea leading the way with seven catches and 34 yards, as part of Taylor Mouser opting for a quicker, shorter, passing attack. Offensive Line: C Not the worst, but not the greatest performance ever for this group. Let’s just cut the difference and call it a C. Defensive Line: D Once again, there was a lack of pressure generated from the front lines, not to mention how badly they got pushed around once Bryce Underwood got benched. Linebacker: C Poor Tony Rojas, he could have been balling out at Miami right now helping the Hurricanes get back to the national championship game and win it all this time around. Instead, he’s stuck with putting together performances like his team-leading 12 total tackles, including two for a loss and a sack in yet another losing effort. Secondary: A- Michigan was held to just 90 yards passing, as Zion Tracy had an interception off a wild ricochet and Josiah Zayas had an Odell Beckham Jr.-like pick right before halftime to snuff out what likely would’ve been a scoring drive for Michigan. Speaking of Zayas, the true freshman has been one of the few bright spots on this team and deserves the biggest bag possible to keep him around in Happy Valley. Special Teams: B+ Ryan Barker nailed his lone field goal attempt and Nathan Tiyce had a couple of nice punts to pin Michigan deep in their own red zone. Coaching: F Hey, did you know if your starting quarterback is struggling, looking incompetent, and absolutely holding your team back, you can bench him for somebody else? Kyle Whittingham got that memo, but apparently Matt Campbell didn’t.

item.title: Nottingham Forest v Arsenal: Premier League – live
item.description: ⚽ Updates from the City Ground; kick-off 4.30pm BST ⚽ Scores | Tables | Read Football Daily | Mail Daniel Forest will want – and probably need – to make this game a mess. If it’s open and played through midfield, Arsenal will open them up because, with the guile they’ve added by buying Guimaraes, along with an in-form Odegaard, they have the ability to exploit space. For that reason, Forest need bodies everywhere, especially in the middle of the pitch, forcing them wide, where Saka might just’ve lost the spring in his acceleration following last season’s achilles injury while, on the other side, Eze isn’t going to go on the outside. Elsewhere, 10-man Sunderland trail Bournemouth 2-0 with seconds remaining, while Brighton have splattered Palace 5-0 to move second above Arsenal, their goal difference +18. Ridiculous behaviour. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester United miss chance to make statement after turbulent week with draw at Leeds
item.description: A 1-1 draw at Elland Road in January 2026 for a Manchester United side with a back three and framed by some incendiary comments about Jason Wilcox precipitated the departure of a manager. A repeat result is less likely to bring the same outcome, not least because Michael Carrick was not the one criticising the director of football. Yet when it seemed Carrick might be turning a corner, that his side were set for their finest result of a stuttering season and that his players were, as he claimed, galvanised by the events of the last week , United lost another lead and the chance to deliver a statement on the pitch. Compared to the injury-time goals Everton and Tottenham scored, at least there was no late letdown for United – not with Noussair Mazraoui clearing off the line from Anton Stach in the 92nd minute – but they can summon different types of disappointment. Even as, after adopting Ruben Amorim ’s favourite system – probably not a tribute to the Portuguese, even if his valedictory game came against Leeds – they looked more solid in open play, they have now conceded three set-piece goals in Yorkshire already this season, including Dominic Calvert-Lewin ’s equaliser. It is a reason why their wait for a Premier League clean sheet goes on. And, indeed, why their wait for a win does. They have shared the points in their last three top-flight games but, in all competitions, they are without a victory in six matches. Even Amorim never went six without winning, if a triumph on penalties is factored in. “We are not getting too carried away, because we didn’t win, but if you keep doing the right things for the right reasons you get what you deserve in the end,” said Carrick. “It wasn't a perfect performance, it wasn't our most unbelievable performance, but there was definitely a lot in there that you can show how together the group were. It felt like a fresh start today.” But without the result which would have demonstrated that. So it did not get worse for Carrick, though there was insufficient evidence to argue it got much better. United had too little threat after conceding. They did not have that much before, either, but at least there was some solidity in a 3-4-3 system, with a back three shielded by twin defensive midfielders. Dominic Calvert-Lewin sealed a point for Leeds (Getty) A half-time lead lent itself to the suggestion their players should criticise Jason Wilcox more often. Two of the players bought by Wilcox combined for the goal. Perhaps, deep in the defence, Lisandro Martinez was celebrating the recruitment he had lamented. But the Argentinian’s eventful week came to an early, and anticlimactic, end as he went off at half-time; if nothing else, that may have spared him the post-match interviews. item.content:encoded: A 1-1 draw at Elland Road in January 2026 for a Manchester United side with a back three and framed by some incendiary comments about Jason Wilcox precipitated the departure of a manager. A repeat result is less likely to bring the same outcome, not least because Michael Carrick was not the one criticising the director of football. Yet when it seemed Carrick might be turning a corner, that his side were set for their finest result of a stuttering season and that his players were, as he claimed, galvanised by the events of the last week , United lost another lead and the chance to deliver a statement on the pitch. Compared to the injury-time goals Everton and Tottenham scored, at least there was no late letdown for United – not with Noussair Mazraoui clearing off the line from Anton Stach in the 92nd minute – but they can summon different types of disappointment. Even as, after adopting Ruben Amorim ’s favourite system – probably not a tribute to the Portuguese, even if his valedictory game came against Leeds – they looked more solid in open play, they have now conceded three set-piece goals in Yorkshire already this season, including Dominic Calvert-Lewin ’s equaliser. It is a reason why their wait for a Premier League clean sheet goes on. And, indeed, why their wait for a win does. They have shared the points in their last three top-flight games but, in all competitions, they are without a victory in six matches. Even Amorim never went six without winning, if a triumph on penalties is factored in. “We are not getting too carried away, because we didn’t win, but if you keep doing the right things for the right reasons you get what you deserve in the end,” said Carrick. “It wasn't a perfect performance, it wasn't our most unbelievable performance, but there was definitely a lot in there that you can show how together the group were. It felt like a fresh start today.” But without the result which would have demonstrated that. So it did not get worse for Carrick, though there was insufficient evidence to argue it got much better. United had too little threat after conceding. They did not have that much before, either, but at least there was some solidity in a 3-4-3 system, with a back three shielded by twin defensive midfielders. Dominic Calvert-Lewin sealed a point for Leeds (Getty) A half-time lead lent itself to the suggestion their players should criticise Jason Wilcox more often. Two of the players bought by Wilcox combined for the goal. Perhaps, deep in the defence, Lisandro Martinez was celebrating the recruitment he had lamented. But the Argentinian’s eventful week came to an early, and anticlimactic, end as he went off at half-time; if nothing else, that may have spared him the post-match interviews. United were breached soon after Mazraoui replaced Martinez; even with three centre-backs, none were near Leeds’ likeliest scorer when he got his fourth goal in five games. Calvert-Lewin ran away from Carlos Baleba and held off Bryan Mbeumo when he met Nico Elvedi’s header and hooked in a shot. They had failed to heed the warning from an earlier set-piece from Stach, with Senne Lammens saving Elvedi’s first-half header. And there was a spirit and a resilience to Leeds, now only beaten in six of their last 32 league matches, and only by champions Arsenal this season. Yet they were below their best. “It says a lot that we are even slightly disappointed with a point against Manchester United,” manager Daniel Farke said. “You always have to be aware, it is still Manchester United. Many, many compliments to my players for a dominant performance against Man United.” The outspoken Lisandro Martinez was hooked at half-time (Reuters) He noted the team that switched shape because of the opposition was in fact United. “It says a lot about how much respect we've earned,” the German said. Carrick only called it a “tweak” but it at least offered indications he can change. His United have floundered against sides with a back three, so he borrowed from Amorim’s infamous fondness for the formation. At times, it seemed United had no centre-forward; at others, it was Mbeumo. Youri Tielemans , signed as a central midfielder, has looked better when others play that role. He was in the front three, and integral in the supply line. “I am really impressed with Youri,” Carrick said. United led when Mbeumo poked in a shot from Tielemans’ low centre. The same combination had almost brought an earlier breakthrough, with Tielemans’ quality apparent in the inside-right channel as the unmarked Mbeumo headed wide from the Belgian’s cross. “Bryan gives so much to the team,” said Carrick. With Benjamin Sesko injured, Marcus Rashford unused and Matheus Cunha limited to a cameo, Mbeumo had to. United’s new look was a more defensive one. It still did not lend itself to either a shutout or a victory.

item.title: Did Thunder’s Sam Presti tell Kevin Durant about James Harden trade? The mystery is solved
item.description: DOUG HOKE/THE OKLAHOMAN / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Did Thunder’s Sam Presti tell Kevin Durant about James Harden trade? The mystery is solved appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Sam Presti never gave Kevin Durant a heads-up before trading James Harden to the Houston Rockets in 2012. That’s according to veteran NBA journalist Jonathan Abrams. It seems to have finally answered a question that has lingered over the Oklahoma City Thunder ’s franchise history for more than a decade. Speaking via The NBA Base, Abrams revealed that he directly asked Durant whether Presti had discussed the blockbuster move with him beforehand. Kevin Durant revealed Sam Presti did not consult him before trading James Harden to Houston in 2012, per @Jpdabrams "It’s interesting because I asked Kevin directly whether Presti discussed trading James with him before making the move. Kevin said, 'Sam has probably grown since… pic.twitter.com/GwMppR3nlg — NBABase (@TheNBABase) October 18, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Kevin said, ‘Sam has probably grown since then, but no, back then I just played basketball; he didn’t talk to me about those moves,'” Abrams recalled. The revelation offers a revealing glimpse into Oklahoma City’s front-office philosophy at the time. Fresh off a run to the 2012 NBA Finals, the Thunder appeared poised to contend for years with Durant, Russell Westbrook, and Harden leading the way. Troy Taormina-Imagn Images However, contract negotiations with Harden stalled over approximately $4.5 million. That prompted Presti to trade the reigning Sixth Man of the Year to Houston just before the regular season. The decision reshaped the franchise and helped launch Harden’s rise into an MVP-caliber superstar. Meanwhile, it left Oklahoma City to build around Durant and Westbrook. Presti has since established himself as one of basketball’s most influential executives. After beginning his career with the San Antonio Spurs, he took charge of the Seattle SuperSonics’ front office in 2007 and oversaw the transition to Oklahoma City. His drafting of Durant, Westbrook, and Harden helped propel the Thunder to the Finals. Years later, a new rebuild brought Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Chet Holmgren, and Jalen Williams into the fold. That patient approach culminated in Oklahoma City’s 2025 championship .Kevin Durant has finally shed light on one of the Thunder’s most consequential decisions. Related: Thunder reserve reveals how Chet Holmgren embraces ‘adversity’ ahead of Spurs duel Related: Thunder waive former first-round pick before season opener

item.title: College football top 25 rankings 2026: Coaches Poll released for Week 8
item.description: Week 7 of the 2026 college football season is in the books, and it was another weekend full of unpredictable upsets, especially at the top of the poll, with a record five teams in the top seven suffering defeat. On Sunday morning, the latest Coaches Poll was released to give us a snapshot of how every team stacks up against each other as we prepare to kick off Week 8 of the season. The Miami Hurricanes have taken over the No. 1 overall spot, while Ohio State, BYU, Georgia, and Texas Tech round out the top five. MORE: College football stock up, stock down from Week 7: SEC elite suffer reality check BYU was the big winner, jumping five spots into the top three after upsetting the previously No. 2-ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish, who fell to No. 8. Oct 9, 2026; Provo, Utah, USA; BYU Cougars cheer squad performs between the third and fourth quarter of a game against the Iowa State Cyclones at LaVell Edwards Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Aaron Baker-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The Texas Longhorns, meanwhile, plummeted 12 spots to No. 18 overall, after sitting at No. 1 just two weeks ago. Where does your favorite team stand in the updated Coaches Poll? A full look at the Coaches Poll for Week 8 of the 2026 college football season can be seen below. MORE: ESPN ‘College GameDay’ location announced for Week 8 of 2026 season 2026 Coaches Poll Top 25 rankings- Week 8 Oct 17, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Miami Hurricanes running back Mark Fletcher Jr. (4) celebrates with quarterback Darian Mensah (10) after a touchdown during the first quarter against the Florida State Seminoles at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Miami Ohio State BYU Georgia Texas Tech Indiana Ole Miss Notre Dame Utah UCLA Tennessee Kentucky Alabama Iowa USC Houston LSU Texas Wake Forest SMU Missouri Boise State Northwestern Florida Oregon Schools Dropped Out No. 19 Mississippi State; No. 20 Oklahoma State; Others Receiving Votes Arizona 141; Oklahoma State 87; James Madison 80; Auburn 55; Mississippi State 32; Nebraska 19; Oregon State 17; New Mexico 16; UTSA 13; Michigan 10; North Dakota State 8; Wisconsin 7; Duke 7; North Carolina 5; Pittsburgh 4; Air Force 3; North Texas 1; About the Coaches Poll “The US LBM Coaches Poll is conducted weekly throughout the regular season using a panel of head coaches at Football Bowl Subdivision schools,” USA TODAY writes. “The panel is chosen by random draw, conference by conference plus independents, from a pool of coaches who have indicated to the American Football Coaches Association their willingness to participate. Each coach submits a Top 25 with a first-place vote worth 25 points, second place 24, and so on down to one point for 25th.”

item.title: Jamel Dean Gets Nod as Steelers Captain vs. Former Team
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Jamel Dean in a game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now TAMPA, Fla. — Ahead of Sunday’s road matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, cornerback Jamel Dean and running back Travis Homer served as the Pittsburgh Steelers’ captains at the coin toss. Dean played the first seven seasons of his NFL career with the Buccaneers before signing with Mike McCarthy’s team as a free agent in the offseason. Dean joked earlier this week about having to make sure not to go “on autopilot” and walk into the home locker room at Raymond James Stadium. The Steelers switched to a weekly captain format under McCarthy. “I think Mike believes in … everybody has leadership abilities,” Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said. “And I think there’s gotta be a way to foster that, and it’s great opportunities, for young guys, especially, or special teamers to lead. Because it doesn’t always have to be the best player on the team, or the oldest player on the team, or the guy with the most Pro Bowls, or the guy who’s been on the team the longest to lead. Young players need to step up and lead.” Homer, another offseason addition, made his mark as a special teamer with the Seattle Seahawks and Chicago Bears. Alan Saunders provided reporting from Tampa. Related Headlines Despite Injury Scare, Steelers TE Pat Freiermuth Will Play vs. Tampa Bay Steelers WR Brandon Johnson Leans On Faith in Wandering NFL Journey Massive Test: Bucs Vet DT Vita Vea Stands in Way of Steelers Rushing Success Read more at Steelers Now

item.title: 🔒Tied down: Boca Juniors extend Milton Delgado's contract
item.description: 🔒Tied down: Boca Juniors extend Milton Delgado's contract Boca Juniors have officially confirmed a significant move for their first-team squad by extending the contract of one of their most promising academy graduates, midfielder Milton Delgado. Official signing and improved terms At a club ceremony led by Boca's Sporting Director, Marcelo Delgado, the young footballer put pen to paper on a contract extension that includes a significant pay rise. item.title: Barca defenders Garcia, Kounde doubt for PSG, Real Madrid clash
item.description: Barcelona defenders Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde have sustained injuries ahead of important matches against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League and Real Madrid in La Liga, the Spanish champions said Sunday. Spanish centre-back Garcia will miss both games and spend between “three to four weeks” out with a thigh injury, Barca said in a statement. Right-back Kounde suffered an ankle sprain and Barca said he would miss the trip to face PSG on Tuesday but may still be able to feature in the Clasico on Sunday, October 25, depending on the “evolution of the injury”. Both defenders ended the club’s 5-2 win over Real Betis in La Liga on Saturday with discomfort. Hansi Flick’s side won a ninth consecutive league game to continue their 100 percent start to the campaign. Double-defending European champions PSG announced a defensive absence of their own after Portuguese left-back Nuno Mendes picked up a knock in Saturday’s Ligue 1 win at Strasbourg. “Having sustained an injury to his left thigh during last night’s match against RC Strasbourg Alsace, Nuno Mendes will be sidelined for the next few weeks,” PSG posted on their website. The post Barca defenders Garcia, Kounde doubt for PSG, Real Madrid clash appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: March 28, 2026, Fort Worth, Texas, USA: FORT WORTH, TX : UConn womenÃââ s head basketball coach GENO AURIEMMA addresses the media Saturday morning at Dickies Arena in Fort Worth. Fort Worth USA – ZUMAm257 20260328_zsp_m257_019 Copyright: xBrianxMcLeanx ©IMAGO/ZUMA Press Wire Geno Auriemma, like every coach, appreciates players who understand their roles and do what the team needs without questioning every instruction. But Svetlana Abrosimova was not always that kind of player. And years after their now-hilarious UConn exchange over a screen, the legendary coach has finally revealed exactly how he responded to her unforgettable question. Speaking at the pregame media availability ahead of UConn’s exhibition matchup against Texas, Auriemma reflected on the tendency of most international players to simply execute instructions without pushback, before going back to memory lane with a vivid example of one who was quite the exception. During Svetlana Abrosimova’s time at UConn, Auriemma had called her out for missing a screening assignment, telling her directly that she was supposed to set a screen. And her response was the kind of line that coaches never forget. “Why should I make screen? I am already open.” Still my favorite line of all time. My response was ‘to get somebody else open, you selfish little sh*t,’” Auriemma recalled . Svetlana Abrosimova played under Auriemma at UConn for four seasons, from 1997 to 2001. And during her standout career in Storrs, she helped lead the Huskies to an NCAA National Championship in 2000. Discover the raw, unfiltered side of Geno Auriemma's coaching philosophy through a candid moment with one of his former stars. Subscribe for the stories behind the legend. item.content:encoded: March 28, 2026, Fort Worth, Texas, USA: FORT WORTH, TX : UConn womenÃââ s head basketball coach GENO AURIEMMA addresses the media Saturday morning at Dickies Arena in Fort Worth. Fort Worth USA – ZUMAm257 20260328_zsp_m257_019 Copyright: xBrianxMcLeanx ©IMAGO/ZUMA Press Wire Geno Auriemma, like every coach, appreciates players who understand their roles and do what the team needs without questioning every instruction. But Svetlana Abrosimova was not always that kind of player. And years after their now-hilarious UConn exchange over a screen, the legendary coach has finally revealed exactly how he responded to her unforgettable question. Speaking at the pregame media availability ahead of UConn’s exhibition matchup against Texas, Auriemma reflected on the tendency of most international players to simply execute instructions without pushback, before going back to memory lane with a vivid example of one who was quite the exception. During Svetlana Abrosimova’s time at UConn, Auriemma had called her out for missing a screening assignment, telling her directly that she was supposed to set a screen. And her response was the kind of line that coaches never forget. “Why should I make screen? I am already open.” Still my favorite line of all time. My response was ‘to get somebody else open, you selfish little sh*t,’” Auriemma recalled . Svetlana Abrosimova played under Auriemma at UConn for four seasons, from 1997 to 2001. And during her standout career in Storrs, she helped lead the Huskies to an NCAA National Championship in 2000. Discover the raw, unfiltered side of Geno Auriemma's coaching philosophy through a candid moment with one of his former stars. Subscribe for the stories behind the legend. She also became the first player in UConn women’s basketball history to earn WBCA/Kodak All-American honors in three consecutive seasons: 1999, 2000, and 2001. She won the conference’s top individual honor as a sophomore in 1999 as well. After cementing herself as a UConn legend, Abrosimova was then selected seventh overall in the 2001 WNBA Draft and went on to build an eleven-year professional career in the league. Whatever Auriemma’s frustrations with her screening habits, the talent was never in question. And that particular elite individual ability is something Auriemma now sees echoes of in one of his current players, Blanca Quiñonez. Unlike Abrosimova, however, she is more representative of the international players who readily accept what their coaches ask of them. Geno Auriemma Compared Blanca Quiñonez to UConn Legend Svetlana Abrosimova “These guys that we have right now, for the most part, this is what I want you to do, and they’re like, yeah, yeah. You saw Blanca last year.” For Auriemma, Blanca Quiñonez is the kind of player who absorbs instruction and executes without resistance, unlike Svetlana Abrosimova. However, like the former Huskies star, she possesses the talent and confidence to make a significant impact on the court. Speaking about Quiñonez in an interview last year, Auriemma revealed that he was careful not to rein in what makes her special. He also drew a direct comparison between the young forward and Abrosimova, pointing to similarities in their playing styles and natural abilities. “But I wouldn’t take anything away from her. I wouldn’t tell her, ‘Stop doing this,’ or ‘Stop doing that.’ Not at all. Just need her to constantly be aware of what’s a good decision, what’s a bad decision. She’s got a lot of Svetlana in her. God bless her.” That comparison carries real weight when you look at what Quiñonez produced in her freshman year . During the 2025-26 season, she was the Huskies’ most electrifying presence off the bench: high-energy, aggressive, and consistently impactful despite not starting a single game across 31 appearances. She averaged 10.7 points, 3.1 rebounds, 2.1 assists, and 2.0 steals per game, the latter figure a testament to the kind of intense on-ball pressure she brought every time she stepped on the floor. And the recognition for this performance followed. Quiñonez swept the conference’s individual sub-awards, claiming Big East Freshman of the Year, Big East Sixth Woman of the Year, All-Big East Second Team, and All-Freshman Team honors. For a player who never started a game, it was a remarkable statement of individual impact. She is now heading into her sophomore year, but is currently sidelined and rehabilitating from two offseason shoulder surgeries to repair a torn labrum. The Huskies open their regular season on November 2 against Cornell, and Quiñonez is expected to return to a significantly expanded role as the team’s second-leading returning scorer once she is fully cleared. If last year was the announcement, the second chapter could be something considerably bigger. item.title: NFL Week 6 early games fan discussion
item.description: Houston Texans' Jawhar Jordan (centre) is tackled by Jacksonville Jaguars' DaVon Hamilton (centre left) during the NFL London Games match at Wembley Stadium, London. Picture date: Sunday October 18, 2026. (Photo by Bradley Collyer/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images Before settling in later today for the Buffalo Bills’ game against the Las Vegas Raiders, there’s plenty of action to enjoy in the early window of Week 6 action in the NFL. The Houston Texans just did a solid for the Bills in taking down the Jacksonville Jaguars, and there’s plenty more drama in store in the rest of the early window. The New England Patriots face the New York Jets this afternoon. Can the Jets do Buffalo a favor in handing the Patriots a loss? Anything’s possible when it comes to an AFC East game! In other AFC action, the Cleveland Browns host the Baltimore Ravens, the latter of which will be without quarterback Lamar Jackson for the second straight game. There’s another NFC South battle between the Indianapolis Colts and the Tennessee Titans, and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are hosting the Pittsburgh Steelers. NFL Week 6 1 p.m. EDT window Atlanta Falcons vs. Chicago Bears New England Patriots vs. New York Jets Cleveland Browns vs. Baltimore Ravens Indianapolis Colts vs. Tennessee Titans Tampa Bay Buccaneers vs. Pittsburgh Steelers New York Giants vs. New Orleans Saints Philadelphia Eagles vs. Carolina Panthers Later this afternoon, the Kansas City Chiefs, fresh off their bye, host the Los Angeles Chargers at Arrowhead. It’s a key game for Bills Mafia to peek in on while it unfolds as the Bills and Raiders clash in Vegas. We’ll of course have a dedicated open thread for the Bills game later today. Here’s your open thread for the early afternoon portion of Week 6. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

item.title: Carrick says draw with Leeds felt like a ‘fresh start’ for Man Utd
item.description: Carrick says draw with Leeds felt like a ‘fresh start’ for Man Utd Michael Carrick believes Manchester United’s 1-1 draw with Leeds felt like a “fresh start” as he praised the attitude and response of his players. Carrick was particularly pleased with the impact of United’s midfield duo of Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos, who he feels are adapting well to the demands of playing for the club. “They’re both young players adapting to life at this football club and I thought both of them were terrific today and I thought they both did really well in midweek,” Carrick said. “That’s a massive positive for us.” The United boss felt there was a different mentality around the group heading into the game and was encouraged by the way his players responded. “It felt like a bit of a fresh start, if I’m honest, today, with where we’re at, accepting it and doing something about it,” he said. “It definitely shows that the boys are desperate to do well for each other as much as anything else and how much they appreciate playing for this football club. “There was a real purpose to the group over the last couple of days and they took it onto the pitch. “That’s a tough game today and it can find you out pretty quickly but the boys stood up to it really well.” Carrick admitted United are still some way from where they want to be, but remains convinced they can turn their form around. “We’re not accepting that anything is great by any stretch so I’m realistic with that,” he said. “But sometimes you do struggle and you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet and we’ve got to find a way through it. “There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time where it can go in different directions and we’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.” He added: “I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it a certain way but I’ve got no doubts that we can go on a good run. “If we keep doing the right things I still think we can have a really good season.”

item.title: ADC Campaign to Kwankwaso: Declare for APC if you share its agenda
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has challenged Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso to openly declare for the All Progressives Congress (APC) if he shares its political agenda, accusing him of attacking opposition figures while sparing President Bola Tinubu’s administration. The Council said Kwankwaso, the vice-presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), whose presidential candidate is Peter Obi, should be holding the ruling party accountable for the country’s worsening economic hardship and insecurity rather than repeatedly targeting ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar. In a statement on Sunday, ADC-PCC Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, dismissed Kwankwaso’s response to the Council’s earlier criticism as diversionary, insisting that it failed to address concerns over his political priorities. “Why is Senator Kwankwaso making our candidate the issue instead of confronting the ruling APC, whose policies have made life increasingly difficult for millions of Nigerians?” the Council asked. It listed hunger, insecurity, high fuel prices, the depreciation of the naira and mounting economic hardship among the issues it said should command the attention of opposition politicians. The Council questioned why Kwankwaso’s attacks appeared more frequently directed at Atiku and the ADC than at the APC government over the country’s challenges. “For the avoidance of doubt, the ADC cannot and will not be distracted by Senator Kwankwaso,” it declared. Describing the ADC as an increasingly accepted political platform, the Council said it remained focused on mobilising Nigerians around its promise to rescue the country from what it called the failures of APC governance. It also accused Kwankwaso of seeking political favour from the ruling party through his attacks on the ADC, urging him to demonstrate his political position openly rather than continue targeting the opposition party. The ADC-PCC reaffirmed its commitment to presenting Nigerians with an alternative in the 2027 general election, ending its response with a direct challenge to Kwankwaso: align openly with the APC if he shares its agenda. The post ADC Campaign to Kwankwaso: Declare for APC if you share its agenda appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Northwestern football wins ugly, and that might be the best sign yet
item.description: EAST LANSING, MI - OCTOBER 17: Northwestern Wildcats quarterback Aidan Chiles (0) walks off the field with offensive coordinator Chip Kelly following a college football game between the Michigan State Spartans and Northwestern Wildcats on October 17, 2026 at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing, MI. (Photo by Adam Ruff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Wildcats’ teams of the past drop this game. They’d find a way to lose, usually in the most agonizing manner available. It looked like that was inevitable in the dying moments of this one. And yet, despite failing on a fake punt from its own 28-yard line in a tie game, on the road, against the coach who built the program, the Wildcats won anyway. That tells you most of what you need to know about how this team is different. Michigan State took over with 3:29 left, moved to the NU 15 and sent Liam Boyd out for a 33-yard field goal that should have given the Spartans the lead. The old Northwestern watches that kick go through and starts explaining itself. This Northwestern saw Brendan Flakes’ hand deflect the kick, drove 64 yards in 58 seconds and let Jackson Kleather win it 24-21 from 34 yards with two seconds left. For most of the afternoon, this was not a pretty football game. Michigan State outgained Northwestern 72-13 in the first quarter. The Spartans finished with eight tackles for loss and five sacks. item.content:encoded: EAST LANSING, MI - OCTOBER 17: Northwestern Wildcats quarterback Aidan Chiles (0) walks off the field with offensive coordinator Chip Kelly following a college football game between the Michigan State Spartans and Northwestern Wildcats on October 17, 2026 at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing, MI. (Photo by Adam Ruff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Wildcats’ teams of the past drop this game. They’d find a way to lose, usually in the most agonizing manner available. It looked like that was inevitable in the dying moments of this one. And yet, despite failing on a fake punt from its own 28-yard line in a tie game, on the road, against the coach who built the program, the Wildcats won anyway. That tells you most of what you need to know about how this team is different. Michigan State took over with 3:29 left, moved to the NU 15 and sent Liam Boyd out for a 33-yard field goal that should have given the Spartans the lead. The old Northwestern watches that kick go through and starts explaining itself. This Northwestern saw Brendan Flakes’ hand deflect the kick, drove 64 yards in 58 seconds and let Jackson Kleather win it 24-21 from 34 yards with two seconds left. For most of the afternoon, this was not a pretty football game. Michigan State outgained Northwestern 72-13 in the first quarter. The Spartans finished with eight tackles for loss and five sacks. Their two biggest plays on special teams, a 44-yard kickoff return and a 41-yard punt return, set up touchdowns. Northwestern didn’t lead in the second half until the clock read 0:02. Braun didn’t dress it up afterward. “There were too many missed opportunities there in the first half,” Braun said. “We got to find ways to start cleaner. And I don’t want to say faster.” Caleb Komolafe’s 10-yard run early in the second quarter put Northwestern up 10-7, and the run game had to find its footing in real time on the way to his 67 yards. Komolafe said the fix started on the sideline. “We just got to be better at our keys,” Komolafe said. “You go back to the work that we did on the sideline, fixing things, and we ultimately started to do better.” They did. After that first quarter, Northwestern outgained Michigan State 347-233 and held the ball for nearly 35 minutes. The Wildcats went 5-for-5 in the red zone and converted 7 of 14 third downs while the Spartans managed 3 of 12. Michigan State went for it on fourth down four times and got stopped twice, both inside Northwestern territory. That is what situational football looks like on a stat sheet, and what separates a good football team from a great one. Anybody can beat somebody by 30 when everything is clicking; prevailing on a day when it feels like many things aren’t going right is harder, and in the Big Ten it might be worth more. The counterargument is obvious: Michigan State is 2-5, it’s still finding itself under a first-year coach, and a 33-yard field goal that gets blocked is as much luck as it is resilience. Maybe Northwestern didn’t prove anything beyond the fact that it can beat a bad team in a close game. But the Wildcats were the better team in the moments that decide close games. That’s the same thing Braun has been saying since July. At Big Ten Media Days, he talked about the 88% of returning snaps that chose to stay at Northwestern. “That’s how you win in the fourth quarter in the Big Ten, with a bunch of guys that are going to battle for one another,” Braun said this summer. That sounded like a talking point in July. Saturday looked a lot like the plan. Then there was Aidan Chiles, who spent two years in East Lansing and walked back into Spartan Stadium to a crowd that made sure he knew it. He gained one yard on his first two snaps. A week earlier, asked about the trip, he had looked at the Northwestern media and answered in a flat monotone. “I’m excited. Do I look excited?” Chiles said. He didn’t look like himself early. He held the ball too long on certain snaps, and he was 5-for-10 for 55 yards at the half. “I’m a little disappointed in how we started off,” Chiles said. “But at the end of the day, a win is a win.” Nobody made the storyline THE story. “We weren’t really in the mindset of exterior factors, like former this, former that,” Flakes said. “When we get in the white lines, all we focus on is the job that we have in front of us.” Chiles was a different quarterback after halftime: 13-of-17 for 171 yards, the two-point conversion, and the 64-yard drive in the final minute that set up Kleather’s kick. He put the day in simple terms. “We came here with one mission,” Chiles said, “and we achieved it.” The second quarter offered two chances to extend the lead, and Northwestern let both slip. Chiles put a 23-yard throw right in Drew Wagner’s hands in the end zone and Wagner dropped it. Kleather came out and had his 41-yard try blocked by Eli Coenen. Two chances gone in two plays. Even with that, the Wildcats were able to regroup and not make those mistakes again. On a 14-play, 61-yard drive, Chiles sneaked for two yards on third-and-1 and scrambled for five on third-and-4. Then he bought time in the pocket on third-and-8 and hit Alex Honig for 19. It ended in a Kleather field goal, but it ate 7:32 and kept the ball away from a Spartan team still clinging to a 14-10 lead. Kleather has a phrase for it. “Something we say in our room is birdie after bogey,” Kleather said. “So step up, and if you miss a kick or if something poor happens, you just step up and do your job next time.” Braun said he never needed to say a word to Kleather. “Nothing needed to be said to Jackson,” Braun said. “He’s built for that opportunity.” When Michigan State pushed the lead to 21-13 early in the fourth quarter, Northwestern answered with a four-minute, 77-yard drive. Chiles sneaked it in from the 1 and hit Alex Honig on the two-point conversion to tie it at 21. Chiles said the offense went to tempo and caught Michigan State off guard. “We were going tempo, so it was a little different than huddling, and it was kind of catching them off guard,” Chiles said. “It was nothing special. We just executed how we were supposed to.” Then came the fake punt. Braun needed the same attitude from his team afterward, that no-frills mentality. “We’re not going to operate off a platform of fear,” Braun said. “I certainly made a decision to go with the fake punt that I thought was a good call…and in hindsight it was a horrible decision. But that’s what great teams look like. They have one another’s back. This football team had my back in that.” Komolafe said the sideline lived it in real time. “After we didn’t get the fake, it was just encouraging the defense to go out there and get a stop,” Komolafe said. Special teams looked like the unit most likely to cost NU the game. Then it won it, for the first time this season. “We knew it was going to be a knockout-dragout battle on special teams,” Braun said. Flakes said he felt it coming before the snap when he got his hands on Michigan State’s kick. “I just had a feeling in my body I was going to get the play,” Flakes said. “It was like slow motion. As I put my hand up, I had full vision on the kicker, and I was just floating with my right hand in the air and it went right to my hand.” Braun said the block came from alignments built so that when the hands went up, someone had a chance to touch the ball. Then the offense went to work on a scenario it had also practiced, the two-minute drill with no timeouts. Chiles hit Komolafe and Wilde to get across midfield, then found Wilde again for 17 along the sideline. Komolafe ran to the 16, where Chiles spiked it with five seconds left. “Our guys have been in the furnace in practice scenarios with that so many times you could tell that they were ready for the moment,” Braun said. item.description: October 10, 2026, Lexington, Kentucky, USA: Kentucky fans look on as LSU huddles up for a timeout during the college football game between the Kentucky Wildcats and the LSU Tigers at Kroger Field. ESPN’s Tori Petry learned that the hard way during the Oklahoma Sooners’ clash with Kentucky, as Will Stein stepped in to remind her exactly where his team stands.
