item.title: Georgia’s Kirby Smart reveals Gunner Stockton’s defiant reaction to blowing Auburn game
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Georgia’s Kirby Smart reveals Gunner Stockton’s defiant reaction to blowing Auburn game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Georgia football looked like the clear top-ranked team in college football after taking down Alabama on the road a week ago, but life comes at you fast in this sport. On Saturday, Kirby Smart and the Bulldogs were on the wrong end of a shocking upset, as unranked Auburn took down Georgia 27-24 between the hedges in Athens. Auburn, despite the flaws that it has shown throughout the season, played an excellent game on Saturday in all facets. However, turnovers proved to be the deciding factor that pushed the Tigers over the top . Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton threw a pair of interceptions and gave away a back-breaking fumble in the fourth quarter that allowed Auburn to kick the game-winning field goal. After the game, Smart talked about his quarterback and his reaction to costing his team the game against one of its bitter rivals, via Mark Schlabach of ESPN. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I saw him in the locker room,” Smart said. “His head was up. I mean, we wouldn’t have been in the position we were in if it wasn’t for Gunner. I’m really proud that he’s growing up and getting better. He had all the success last week, and so many people want to reach out and talk about it. It’s tough.” Stockton is usually very solid for Georgia and has been exactly that since he became the starter, so it was a bit surprising to see him be so careless with the football on Saturday. Auburn’s defense has not played very well at any point this season, so that made Georgia’s offensive struggles even more of the surprise. Despite this surprising loss, Georgia will still be very highly ranked and still has all of its goals in front of it this season. There are no unbeaten teams left in the SEC, so a conference title is still on the table for Smart and company. Georgia has a bye week in Week 8. Smart and company will be back in action in Week 9 in a rivalry game against Florida where Stockton will be trying to get back on track. Related: Florida State football loses star running back to injury after crushing Miami loss Related: Alabama OC Ryan Grubb’s resume takes another brutal hit with offensive disaster vs. Tennessee

item.title: When Juventus expects Yildiz to be back in latest update
item.description: When Juventus expects Yildiz to be back in latest update Juventus are still waiting for Kenan Yildiz to return to action after his surgery at the start of the season , with the attacker remaining one of the club’s most important players. His absence has been felt, and the Bianconeri are eager to have him back as they look to remain competitive across all competitions. The club are doing their best to maintain its level while Yildiz continues his recovery. Juventus want to ensure the team remains in a strong position so that his return can provide a boost rather than come with the pressure of rescuing their campaign. Juventus continue to miss Yildiz Yildiz has established himself as a key figure at Juventus and appears comfortable with the expectations that come with his role. His performances have demonstrated his importance to the team, making his absence particularly difficult as the club navigates the season without him. The Bianconeri are counting down to his return, but it appears supporters will need to remain patient. His recovery is expected to take longer than just a few days or weeks, leaving Juventus to manage his absence while he works towards full fitness. According to Tuttojuve , Juventus expect Yildiz to remain sidelined until the start of December. That timeline means his return could still be some way off, depending on how his recovery progresses over the coming weeks. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) The Bianconeri will not rush his recovery There is also a possibility that Yildiz could miss the remainder of the calendar year if his recovery does not go according to plan. Such an outcome would be a significant setback for Juventus, given the influence he has had on the team. However, the club are understood to be unwilling to rush him back before he is ready. While they would welcome his return as soon as possible, ensuring that he recovers properly remains the priority. Juventus believe the final month of the year could be an appropriate target for his comeback. That would give Yildiz more time to complete his rehabilitation and return when he is ready to contribute again. Until then, the Bianconeri must find ways to cope without one of their most important players . His return would provide a welcome boost, but Juventus appear prepared to remain patient rather than risk bringing him back too soon.

item.title: Where is Ohio State football ranked in major polls after Week 7?
item.description: Ohio State has risen in the latest US LBM Coaches Poll . The Buckeyes snapped defending national champion Indiana’s 22-game winning streak in a top-five matchup on Oct. 17, and other unbeatens fell as well over a matter of hours, paving the way to OSU's jump. Georgia and Notre Dame, which were both off to 6-0 starts and the consensus No. 1 and No. 2 teams a week ago, suffered their first losses. Auburn upset the Bulldogs in Athens, while BYU topped the Irish in one of the more high-profile games. Since a loss at Texas in early September, the Buckeyes had not been ranked higher than No. 5 in either the AP Top 25 or US LBM Coaches Poll . The Buckeyes began the season as the preseason No. 1, bolstered by the presence of star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, as well as quarterback Julian Sayin. Here’s where the Buckeyes landed in the latest polls following their 19-15 win at Indiana . Ohio State football rankings after Week 7 US LBM Coaches Poll The Buckeyes are No. 2 behind the new No. 1 Miami (Fla.), which leads the poll for the first time since Dec. 9. 2002. AP Poll To be released. Joey Kaufman covers Ohio State football for The Columbus Dispatch. Email him at jkaufman@dispatch.com and follow him on @joeyrkaufman on X. This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Where is Ohio State football ranked in major polls after Week 7?

item.title: Something unusual stopped the Jaguars-Texans game in London
item.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars-Houston Texans game in London came to an unexpected stop Sunday morning, and it had nothing to do with an injured player. Umpire Larry Smith went down during the first quarter at Wembley Stadium and eventually had to be carted from the field. NBC Sports reported that Smith slipped on the wet grass between plays. Smith fell backward while trying to retrieve the football. He briefly got up but went down again after trying to walk. Trainers from both teams came onto the field before Smith was placed on a cart. He tipped his cap to the Wembley crowd as he left, according to The Sporting News . The NFL was able to keep the game going with six officials instead of the usual seven. NBC Sports reported the league has a system for such situations, with other members of the crew taking over some of the missing umpire’s responsibilities. Smith is in his second NFL season after previously officiating college football and the USFL. Before the injury, Jacksonville and Houston were scoreless. Houston later struck first when quarterback C.J. Stroud connected with tight end Foster Moreau for a 6-yard touchdown . The extra point gave the Texans a 7-0 advantage. Houston won the game 34-31. Houston later struck first when quarterback C.J. Stroud connected with tight end Foster Moreau for a 6-yard touchdown . The extra point gave the Texans a 7-0 advantage. Houston won the game 34-31. item.title: 8 Mass Effect Replay Ideas That Make the Trilogy Feel Brand-New
item.description: Every replay of the Mass Effect games tends to start with a promise: this time, you’ll do things differently. Then Shepard makes the same speech, you bring the same squad, and you’re right back where you started. BioWare’s Mass Effect Legendary Edition , the remastered trilogy released in May 2021, makes starting over easy. But the best replay value is in changing the rules. Swap the class you always play, tank a choice on purpose, or finish the whole thing with one gun. These eight runs each come with their own mission parameters. And this time, maybe you’ll really do things differently.

item.title: Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog “employee-like” access
item.description: Anthropic has granted external evaluators “employee-like access” to assess the risks of its models, following through on a commitment to increase safeguards over concerns the technology could run catastrophically out of control. METR, a nonprofit that has worked with leading labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, now has a team embedded in the Claude maker’s office with access to its hardware and internal systems. A greater role for third-party evaluators is among the main concrete steps the labs have proposed in response to rising concern about the dangers more capable AI systems could pose to the economy, cyber security and humanity at large. Read full article Comments

item.title: Shettima lists federal projects worth billions in Bauchi
item.description: — BASFA puts value of interventions at ₦144bn By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi Vice-President Kashim Shettima has highlighted federal government projects worth billions of naira in Bauchi State, describing them as evidence of President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to infrastructural development in the North-East. Shettima spoke at the weekend during the inauguration of the Bauchi Shettima Forum for Asiwaju (BASFA) in Bauchi. He was represented at the event by the Minister of State for Regional Development, Uba Maigari Ahmadu. The vice-president said several projects were being implemented through the North-East Development Commission (NEDC) to address the region’s developmental challenges, adding that more projects would be inaugurated in Bauchi and other North-East states in the coming months. He cited the ongoing construction of the Akwanga-Jos-Bauchi-Borno road as a major federal infrastructure project expected to improve connectivity and stimulate economic activities. According to him, the road is being constructed with reinforced concrete to ensure durability. “Work is currently ongoing on this project, utilising modern construction techniques. It is a high-quality road being built with reinforced concrete. We are actively working on it, and I can assure you that construction will reach Bauchi town very soon,” he said. Shettima attributed the administration’s regional development initiatives to the establishment of the Ministry of Regional Development and five regional development commissions to address the peculiar needs of different parts of the country. He urged Bauchi residents to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, saying the ongoing interventions demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to the region’s development. Earlier, the convener of BASFA, Dr Nafi’a M. Abdullahi, said the forum was established to promote awareness of the Tinubu administration’s policies and programmes and highlight its impact on the people of Bauchi State. Abdullahi said the group would mobilise support for the Tinubu-Shettima ticket ahead of the 2027 presidential election, citing projects in healthcare, education, security and agriculture. He cited the ongoing construction of the Akwanga-Jos-Bauchi-Borno road as a major federal infrastructure project expected to improve connectivity and stimulate economic activities. According to him, the road is being constructed with reinforced concrete to ensure durability. “Work is currently ongoing on this project, utilising modern construction techniques. It is a high-quality road being built with reinforced concrete. We are actively working on it, and I can assure you that construction will reach Bauchi town very soon,” he said. Shettima attributed the administration’s regional development initiatives to the establishment of the Ministry of Regional Development and five regional development commissions to address the peculiar needs of different parts of the country. He urged Bauchi residents to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, saying the ongoing interventions demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to the region’s development. Earlier, the convener of BASFA, Dr Nafi’a M. Abdullahi, said the forum was established to promote awareness of the Tinubu administration’s policies and programmes and highlight its impact on the people of Bauchi State. Abdullahi said the group would mobilise support for the Tinubu-Shettima ticket ahead of the 2027 presidential election, citing projects in healthcare, education, security and agriculture. Healthcare, education projects The BASFA convener listed the establishment of a diagnostic centre at the Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital (ATBUTH) and the construction and renovation of eight healthcare facilities across the state among interventions attributed to the NEDC. She also disclosed that efforts were underway to upgrade the General Hospital in Alkaleri to a Federal Medical Centre to expand access to healthcare services. In the education sector, Abdullahi cited the completion of a student hostel at Sa’adu Zungur University, Gadau, and the ongoing construction of 1,600-bed accommodation facilities at the Federal Polytechnic, Bauchi, and Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University (ATBU). She added that the NEDC had established mega schools and renovated educational institutions across the state. On security, Abdullahi said the Federal Government had approved the establishment of military battalions in Alkaleri and Tafawa Balewa to strengthen security and address threats facing communities. She also said the administration had committed resources to agriculture and food production, putting the estimated value of federal projects and interventions in Bauchi at ₦144 billion. Abdullahi said BASFA would continue to promote the administration’s programmes while identifying challenges affecting communities and working with relevant stakeholders to seek solutions. item.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu in Israel’s upcoming election
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Sunday offered his “complete and total” endorsement of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the country’s October 27 elections. “Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel. BIBI NETANYAHU WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN!,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister who is in a tight race to win a new mandate, quickly acknowledged Trump’s gesture. “Thank you, President Trump, for your tremendous support and for our work together. Together we will complete the mission!” Netanyahu wrote on X. In his post, Trump described Netanyahu as “a Great Warrior Prime Minister” and ally in the war against Iran that began in late February with a massive bombing campaign but has dragged on as Tehran has retaliated by blocking global energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz. Trump asserted that without Netanyahu as Israel’s leader, the United States would be alone in combating the threat from the Islamic regime, “with its 51 year old chant, ‘Death to Israel, Death to America! We will destroy the Little Satan and the Big Satan.'” “If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so,” the US president said. “This is the kind of Partner that the United States of America is demanding of Israel, a Country for which it has done so much,” he added. msp/md The post Trump endorses Netanyahu in Israel’s upcoming election appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Computer scientist Margaret Hamilton was a problem-solver for the ages (op-ed)
item.description: null Dean Robbins is a journalist and children's author. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton , who died on Sept. 30 at age 90, played a key role in putting astronauts on the moon. She was a problem-solver extraordinaire, and it all started in early childhood. Considering the name "daddy longlegs" unfair to female arachnids, young Margaret decided to call half of them "mommy longlegs." Wondering why the neighborhood baseball players were all boys, she determined to join the team herself. As she grew up in the 1940s and '50s, Margaret noticed a similar problem with various professions. Why were doctors, judges and scientists almost always men? The solution: she would study hard in school and prepare herself for any job she might care to do. It's no surprise that a born problem-solver would gravitate to computers. In the late 1950s, the new technology offered mind-bending possibilities, and this college math major saw a chance to put her skills to use on a cosmic scale. Hamilton had long been a stargazer, thanks to a philosophical father who taught her to love the night sky . In 1965, after stints in meteorology and satellite tracking, she became interested in a Massachusetts Institute of Technology project that designed in-flight computers for NASA's moon mission. The team, of course, consisted solely of men. But, just as with her neighborhood baseball team, Hamilton refused to accept limitations for herself or anybody else. She kicked open the door and quickly rose to director of software engineering. With her knack for devising novel solutions to seemingly insoluble problems, no one was better suited for the job. Working with the era's primitive technology, Margaret thought through the various mishaps that could occur on a spaceflight and designed the software to handle every contingency. The epochal Apollo 11 moon mission of 1969 put her planning to the test. As astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin neared the moon's surface in their lunar module, an error overloaded the onboard computer's processing unit. Mission Control faced the prospect of aborting the landing, but Margaret's ingenious programming allowed the system to prioritize essential tasks while canceling the inessential ones. The lunar module touched down without a hitch, and Armstrong and Aldrin became famous. An excerpt from Dean Robbins' 2017 book "Margaret and the Moon: How Margaret Hamilton Saved the First Lunar Landing." item.dc:creator: Dean Robbins
item.content:encoded: null Dean Robbins is a journalist and children's author. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton , who died on Sept. 30 at age 90, played a key role in putting astronauts on the moon. She was a problem-solver extraordinaire, and it all started in early childhood. Considering the name "daddy longlegs" unfair to female arachnids, young Margaret decided to call half of them "mommy longlegs." Wondering why the neighborhood baseball players were all boys, she determined to join the team herself. As she grew up in the 1940s and '50s, Margaret noticed a similar problem with various professions. Why were doctors, judges and scientists almost always men? The solution: she would study hard in school and prepare herself for any job she might care to do. It's no surprise that a born problem-solver would gravitate to computers. In the late 1950s, the new technology offered mind-bending possibilities, and this college math major saw a chance to put her skills to use on a cosmic scale. Hamilton had long been a stargazer, thanks to a philosophical father who taught her to love the night sky . In 1965, after stints in meteorology and satellite tracking, she became interested in a Massachusetts Institute of Technology project that designed in-flight computers for NASA's moon mission. The team, of course, consisted solely of men. But, just as with her neighborhood baseball team, Hamilton refused to accept limitations for herself or anybody else. She kicked open the door and quickly rose to director of software engineering. With her knack for devising novel solutions to seemingly insoluble problems, no one was better suited for the job. Working with the era's primitive technology, Margaret thought through the various mishaps that could occur on a spaceflight and designed the software to handle every contingency. The epochal Apollo 11 moon mission of 1969 put her planning to the test. As astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin neared the moon's surface in their lunar module, an error overloaded the onboard computer's processing unit. Mission Control faced the prospect of aborting the landing, but Margaret's ingenious programming allowed the system to prioritize essential tasks while canceling the inessential ones. The lunar module touched down without a hitch, and Armstrong and Aldrin became famous. An excerpt from Dean Robbins' 2017 book "Margaret and the Moon: How Margaret Hamilton Saved the First Lunar Landing." (Image credit: Illustrations by Lucy Knisley, illustrations copyright © 2017 by Lucy Knisley; and Excerpt(s) from MARGARET AND THE MOON by Dean Robbins, text copyright © 2017 by Dean Robbins. Used by permission of Alfred A. Knopf, an imprint of Random House Children's Books, a division of Penguin Random House LLC. All rights reserved.) Sadly, Margaret Hamilton did not. She continued to work behind the scenes, contributing to the five additional lunar landings as well as Skylab and the space shuttle . In 1976, she struck off on her own to start a software company. She might have lived the rest of her life in obscurity if not for a fateful black-and-white photograph from 1969. This image began to attract attention on the internet in the 2010s. It showed Margaret wedged between a coatrack and a blackboard at MIT, standing beside a towering stack of her printed code from the Apollo missions. Bespectacled and smiling, she radiates the confidence of a scientist who had stormed the boys' club and conquered the universe . I was one of those fascinated by the photograph, and I contacted Margaret about the possibility of profiling her in a children's book. She initially resisted, uncomfortable with being the center of attention. But she came to see the appeal of a book about herself that she could read to her great-grandchildren, so that they might be inspired to break barriers themselves one day. She warmed to the task of telling her life story and even sent me examples of her Apollo code, which Lucy Knisley incorporated in the illustrations for " Margaret and the Moon: How Margaret Hamilton Saved the First Lunar Landing ." Another few pages from "Margaret and the Moon." (Image credit: Illustrations by Lucy Knisley, illustrations copyright © 2017 by Lucy Knisley; and Excerpt(s) from MARGARET AND THE MOON by Dean Robbins, text copyright © 2017 by Dean Robbins. Used by permission of Alfred A. Knopf, an imprint of Random House Children's Books, a division of Penguin Random House LLC. All rights reserved.) With the 2016 book and movie " Hidden Figures " calling attention to women's overlooked contributions to the space program, Hamilton soon had to get used to being the center of attention. She received a Presidential Medal of Freedom and achieved LEGO immortality in the "Women of NASA" set. In 2019, to mark the 50th anniversary of the first moon landing , Google used reflected moonlight to create a massive portrait of Margaret in the Mojave Desert. Rarely has so humble a soul received so grand a tribute. The world will miss Margaret Hamilton, but, just like her great-grandchildren, we will always have her example to inspire us. She showed that, no matter how daunting the obstacles, there are few problems we can't solve.

item.title: Buhari saw Tinubu as ‘Bad News’ for Nigeria — Baba-Ahmed
item.description: — PRP chairman says ex-president resisted pressure to back Tinubu in 2023 Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, national chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), has claimed that former President Muhammadu Buhari was reluctant to transfer power to President Bola Tinubu in 2023 because he considered him “bad news” for Nigeria. Baba-Ahmed spoke at a summit organised by the Northern Elders Forum, in a video published on Symfoni’s YouTube channel on Saturday. He said Nigerians should have questioned Tinubu’s presidential ambition when he declared “Emilokan”, meaning “it is my turn”, during the build-up to the 2023 general election. “Nigerians ought to have known there was something wrong the day Tinubu said, ‘It’s my turn’. Maybe we missed it,” he said. “We have a presidency of a country of 250 million people. My turn? To do what? To become president.” Baba-Ahmed said Buhari was reluctant to hand over power to Tinubu after considering the implications of his presidency for the country. “Even Buhari saw Tinubu as bad news for this country. In fairness to him, he is not around him. Buhari resisted some people who insisted it had to be Tinubu,” he said. The PRP chairman criticised Tinubu’s administration, alleging that the country had deteriorated under his leadership. “Now we are being depressed for having a president for three and a half years. He has dragged the country as low as it is possible to go. And it has to stop him. We cannot go below, beyond where we are,” Baba-Ahmed said. He, however, expressed confidence in Nigerians’ ability to overcome the country’s challenges, saying the nation had survived major crises in the past. “We are very resilient people. We have seen crises bigger than this, and we survived it. We survived it, and we will survive this one,” he said. “We will survive the four years of abuse, neglect, and plunder that Tinubu has caused because Nigeria has to survive for our children and their children.” ‘Every index of failure shows in this administration’ Baba-Ahmed accused Tinubu of prioritising his political ambition over the welfare of Nigerians, alleging that the administration had failed across key indicators. “We will not allow a president to fulfil an ambition that one individual alone can wreck his country, just to prove that he has the power and the money to do so,” he said. “We are at the bottom. There is no way to go anymore. Every index of failure shows in this administration.” He also faulted Tinubu for not personally appealing to Nigerians for another term, saying the president had instead relied on political allies to campaign on his behalf. Baba-Ahmed further accused northern governors of failing to draw the president’s attention to economic hardship and public dissatisfaction in the region. Baba-Ahmed further accused northern governors of failing to draw the president’s attention to economic hardship and public dissatisfaction in the region. Opposition coalition targets 2027 election The PRP chairman said opposition parties were working towards forming a coalition to challenge Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. He described the effort as serious, saying the parties were prepared to pool resources and set aside their differences to build a common front. “What we have seen is an incredible willingness for politicians to come together and say, let’s put aside some of our differences and see if we can actually create a momentum strong enough to remove this Tinubu,” he said. Baba-Ahmed said the coalition would produce a candidate to challenge the president and urged Nigerians opposed to Tinubu’s re-election bid to support whoever emerged as its flag-bearer. “There will be a candidate that will be produced by this coalition. Vote for whoever he is,” he said. He also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to ensure that the 2027 general election reflected the will of voters. “INEC must guarantee that the 2027 elections will reflect the will of the people,” he said. “If it does, and it must, because the consequences are almost clear, Tinubu is done.” The post Buhari saw Tinubu as ‘Bad News’ for Nigeria — Baba-Ahmed appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Speaker Abbas mobilises grassroots support for Tinubu, APC candidates in Kaduna
item.description: Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, has urged Kaduna citizens to re-elect President Bola Tinubu and all APC candidates to sustain ongoing reforms and development projects in the state. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that Abbas made the call on Sunday in continuation of the tour of his constituency to inaugurate projects. Speaking during a groundbreaking ceremony for road construction and educational projects in Ikara Local Government Area, Abbas said the sacrifices associated with the Federal Government’s reforms were temporary. He expressed optimism that Nigerians would soon begin to experience the benefits. He urged Nigerians to give Tinubu a second term to complete the reforms, calling him a friend of Kaduna State. The Speaker said Kaduna benefited from four federal university projects within three years under Tinubu’s administration, after decades without another federal university. He listed the upgrade of the Federal College of Education, Zaria, to a university, the establishment of the University of Applied Sciences in Kachia and the conversion of the Kaduna petroleum institute into a university. Abbas also said a bill he sponsored secured presidential approval to convert Kaduna Polytechnic into a Federal University of Technology. He said the development, along with other federal projects, justified Kaduna residents supporting Tinubu’s re-election bid. Abbas also urged residents to support Gov. Uba Sani’s re-election in 2027, citing ongoing road, water and health projects across the state. He warned that a change of government could jeopardise the completion of ongoing projects, urging citizens to support continuity. The Speaker commended Uba Sani for his contributions to Kaduna State’s development and support for his emergence as Speaker of the House of Representatives. He also solicited support for the APC candidates in Kaduna, thanking the party for its support and contributions to development in the state. In his remarks, Gov. Uba Sani, represented by the Secretary to the State Government, Dr AbdulKadir Meyere, commended the Speaker for extending development projects to communities across the state. Gov. Sani also solicited support for all APC candidates in the state for continuity and to sustain the dividends of democracy. The post Speaker Abbas mobilises grassroots support for Tinubu, APC candidates in Kaduna appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Falana warns Ekiti youth against internet fraud
item.description: — Urges governments to tackle illiteracy, unemployment, insecurity By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Human rights lawyer, Femi Falana, SAN, has warned youths in Ekiti State against internet fraud, urging them to use technology productively while calling on the Federal and state governments to intensify efforts to tackle illiteracy, unemployment and insecurity. Falana spoke at the third edition of Afe Babalola Day, held at Afe Babalola University, Ado-Ekiti (ABUAD), where he said Nigeria’s development challenges required urgent and sustained government intervention rather than an overconcentration on political campaigns. At the event, themed “A Celebration of Life, Legacy, Service and Impact” in honour of Aare Afe Babalola, Falana urged young Nigerians to draw inspiration from the legal icon’s life, saying determination, education and the productive use of available opportunities could help them overcome personal and societal limitations. He, however, stressed that individual efforts could not replace the government’s primary responsibility to provide education, infrastructure and an enabling environment for citizens to thrive. Falana expressed concern over the state of basic education in Nigeria, particularly the reported failure of some state governments to access or utilise funds provided through the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC). He said the situation was troubling given the continued prevalence of child and adult illiteracy, despite the adoption of the Child Rights Act across the states and its provisions on children’s access to basic education. The lawyer urged governments to demonstrate greater commitment to education by ensuring that available funds were effectively deployed to improve school enrolment, learning conditions and educational outcomes. Babalola’s life an inspiration, says Falana Falana described Babalola’s achievements as exceptional, citing his rise from a modest formal educational background to becoming one of Nigeria’s most distinguished lawyers as an example of determination, self-development and commitment to excellence. According to him, Babalola pursued further studies through correspondence education, obtained university degrees and qualified to practise law in both England and Nigeria before attaining the rank of Senior Advocate of Nigeria. He said: “I am here to honour Aare Afe Babalola and all other Nigerians who have distinguished themselves in one way or another. Aare Afe Babalola’s achievements are exceptional and rare. “In terms of formal education, the highest level he attained in conventional schooling was Standard Six. However, through correspondence studies, he acquired a Bachelor of Science (BSc) degree and an LLB degree before becoming a lawyer. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: — Urges governments to tackle illiteracy, unemployment, insecurity By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Human rights lawyer, Femi Falana, SAN, has warned youths in Ekiti State against internet fraud, urging them to use technology productively while calling on the Federal and state governments to intensify efforts to tackle illiteracy, unemployment and insecurity. Falana spoke at the third edition of Afe Babalola Day, held at Afe Babalola University, Ado-Ekiti (ABUAD), where he said Nigeria’s development challenges required urgent and sustained government intervention rather than an overconcentration on political campaigns. At the event, themed “A Celebration of Life, Legacy, Service and Impact” in honour of Aare Afe Babalola, Falana urged young Nigerians to draw inspiration from the legal icon’s life, saying determination, education and the productive use of available opportunities could help them overcome personal and societal limitations. He, however, stressed that individual efforts could not replace the government’s primary responsibility to provide education, infrastructure and an enabling environment for citizens to thrive. Falana expressed concern over the state of basic education in Nigeria, particularly the reported failure of some state governments to access or utilise funds provided through the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC). He said the situation was troubling given the continued prevalence of child and adult illiteracy, despite the adoption of the Child Rights Act across the states and its provisions on children’s access to basic education. The lawyer urged governments to demonstrate greater commitment to education by ensuring that available funds were effectively deployed to improve school enrolment, learning conditions and educational outcomes. Babalola’s life an inspiration, says Falana Falana described Babalola’s achievements as exceptional, citing his rise from a modest formal educational background to becoming one of Nigeria’s most distinguished lawyers as an example of determination, self-development and commitment to excellence. According to him, Babalola pursued further studies through correspondence education, obtained university degrees and qualified to practise law in both England and Nigeria before attaining the rank of Senior Advocate of Nigeria. He said: “I am here to honour Aare Afe Babalola and all other Nigerians who have distinguished themselves in one way or another. Aare Afe Babalola’s achievements are exceptional and rare. “In terms of formal education, the highest level he attained in conventional schooling was Standard Six. However, through correspondence studies, he acquired a Bachelor of Science (BSc) degree and an LLB degree before becoming a lawyer. He was called to both the English Bar and the Nigerian Bar and eventually reached the pinnacle of his legal career as a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN). “He has also produced many Senior Advocates of Nigeria, including two of his own children. His life and achievements therefore serve as an inspiration and a model for young people to emulate.” Governments must tackle illiteracy, insecurity Falana said educating Nigerians remained the primary responsibility of government, noting that the Child Rights Act made basic education free and compulsory from primary school to junior secondary school. “Unfortunately, billions of naira released to state governments by the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) remain unutilised, while about ₦65 billion has reportedly not been accessed by state governments and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT),” he said. The lawyer lamented that political campaigns appeared to be taking precedence over efforts to address underdevelopment, illiteracy and youth unemployment. “The only thing going on in the country today appears to be political campaigns, while we are failing to address the problems of underdevelopment, child illiteracy, adult illiteracy and youth unemployment. “We are also grappling with electricity shortages, food insecurity, physical insecurity and social insecurity,” he said. Falana said his travels across the country had left him concerned about the level of development, adding that government had the primary responsibility to provide and maintain infrastructure, including roads and hospitals. “Individuals such as Chief Afe Babalola can only contribute their own quota; the primary responsibility for addressing the problems of underdevelopment in our country rests with the government,” he said. Falana cautions youths, parents against internet fraud The human rights lawyer also used the occasion to warn young people and their parents against internet fraud, which he said was prevalent in Ekiti State. “I have also taken advantage of this programme to warn young people, as well as their parents, against internet fraud, which is very prevalent here. “Young people should take advantage of technology to develop new ideas and pursue productive ventures rather than engage in criminal activities,” he said. Falana also criticised an organisation he identified as the “Iya Omo Ologo” Association in Ekiti State, questioning its reported role in promoting young people allegedly involved in criminal activities. “I understand that there is an organisation called the ‘Iya Omo Ologo’ Association in Ekiti State. It is a shame that such an organisation exists. The members of that organisation must be identified and made to justify how they can come together to promote young people who have engaged in criminality,” he said. He added, however, that government also had a responsibility to engage young people productively and provide opportunities for them to contribute meaningfully to society. Babalola, Ewi call for service, integrity In his remarks, Aare Afe Babalola expressed appreciation to the organisers for the honour, describing the recognition as an encouragement to continue contributing to the development of education and society. The legal luminary thanked the organisers and other distinguished Nigerians who gathered to celebrate his life, legacy and contributions to national development. He also urged young people to embrace hard work, integrity, discipline and commitment to excellence as essential ingredients for success and meaningful contributions to society. Earlier, the Ewi of Ado-Ekiti, Oba Rufus Adejugbe, commended Babalola for his contributions to societal development and humanity, describing his impact as a lasting legacy worthy of celebration and emulation. item.title: Dele Cole: Nigeria has lost one of its finest intellectuals — Obasanjo
item.description: — Says late ambassador helped rebuild Nigeria’s international relations By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has mourned the death of Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, describing him as one of Nigeria’s finest intellectuals and a trusted ally whose contributions to the country’s diplomacy, politics and public service were immense. Obasanjo, in a tribute to the late diplomat, said Cole’s death at the age of 86 was a profound personal loss and a significant loss to Nigeria, particularly given his contributions to the country’s foreign policy and international relations. The former president recalled that his relationship with Cole dated back several decades, when he was military Head of State and the late diplomat worked in the Cabinet Office. Their relationship deepened during Obasanjo’s civilian administration from 1999 to 2007, when Cole served as his Special Adviser on International Relations. Describing Cole as an indispensable member of his administration’s foreign policy team, Obasanjo said the late diplomat played a significant role in efforts to restore Nigeria’s international standing after years of diplomatic isolation. “Nigeria has lost one of its finest intellectual pillars, and I have lost a trusted ally whose counsel shaped pivotal moments in our nation’s history,” he said. Obasanjo explained that when he assumed office in 1999, his administration faced the challenge of reintegrating Nigeria into the international community, making Cole’s diplomatic expertise particularly valuable. “When I took office in 1999, Nigeria was emerging from isolation and desperately needed to be reintegrated into the global community. I knew I needed the finest diplomatic minds beside me, which led to his appointment as my Special Adviser on International Relations,” he said. The former president noted that advising a president with a strong personal interest in foreign policy required exceptional diplomatic skills, adding that Cole’s sophisticated understanding of international affairs made him a crucial member of his administration. According to Obasanjo, Cole travelled extensively with him on official engagements and worked behind the scenes to rebuild Nigeria’s diplomatic relationships and advance the country’s international interests. He also credited the late diplomat with contributing to the diplomatic and economic strategies that culminated in Nigeria’s historic Paris Club debt relief, describing his input as a combination of tact, economic insight and patriotism. “Dele brought unmatched tact, brilliant economic insight, and unyielding patriotism to the table,” Obasanjo said. item.content:encoded: — Says late ambassador helped rebuild Nigeria’s international relations By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has mourned the death of Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, describing him as one of Nigeria’s finest intellectuals and a trusted ally whose contributions to the country’s diplomacy, politics and public service were immense. Obasanjo, in a tribute to the late diplomat, said Cole’s death at the age of 86 was a profound personal loss and a significant loss to Nigeria, particularly given his contributions to the country’s foreign policy and international relations. The former president recalled that his relationship with Cole dated back several decades, when he was military Head of State and the late diplomat worked in the Cabinet Office. Their relationship deepened during Obasanjo’s civilian administration from 1999 to 2007, when Cole served as his Special Adviser on International Relations. Describing Cole as an indispensable member of his administration’s foreign policy team, Obasanjo said the late diplomat played a significant role in efforts to restore Nigeria’s international standing after years of diplomatic isolation. “Nigeria has lost one of its finest intellectual pillars, and I have lost a trusted ally whose counsel shaped pivotal moments in our nation’s history,” he said. Obasanjo explained that when he assumed office in 1999, his administration faced the challenge of reintegrating Nigeria into the international community, making Cole’s diplomatic expertise particularly valuable. “When I took office in 1999, Nigeria was emerging from isolation and desperately needed to be reintegrated into the global community. I knew I needed the finest diplomatic minds beside me, which led to his appointment as my Special Adviser on International Relations,” he said. The former president noted that advising a president with a strong personal interest in foreign policy required exceptional diplomatic skills, adding that Cole’s sophisticated understanding of international affairs made him a crucial member of his administration. According to Obasanjo, Cole travelled extensively with him on official engagements and worked behind the scenes to rebuild Nigeria’s diplomatic relationships and advance the country’s international interests. He also credited the late diplomat with contributing to the diplomatic and economic strategies that culminated in Nigeria’s historic Paris Club debt relief, describing his input as a combination of tact, economic insight and patriotism. “Dele brought unmatched tact, brilliant economic insight, and unyielding patriotism to the table,” Obasanjo said. Beyond his diplomatic responsibilities, the former president highlighted Cole’s contributions to journalism, particularly his tenure as managing director of the Daily Times, where he introduced an independent editorial board system intended to protect editorial policy from political interference. Obasanjo also recalled Cole’s service as Nigeria’s ambassador to Brazil and Argentina, describing his diplomatic assignments and media career as evidence of a life devoted to public service. “His masterful stints as Nigeria’s Ambassador to Brazil and Argentina further cemented his legacy as a titan of public service who proved that integrity and public duty can coexist beautifully,” he said. The former president expressed particular sadness over Cole’s death, which came years after the loss of his wife, Pastor Mina Dugoabere Cole, whom Obasanjo described as the family’s matriarch. He said the deaths of both parents had left a painful void in the Cole family, while expressing hope that they had been reunited in eternity. Obasanjo also offered words of encouragement to the deceased’s children, including Tonye and his siblings, urging them to remain united and preserve their father’s values. “To his children, Tonye and his siblings, my fatherly advice is to stand firm, united, and proud. The greatest monument you can build in honour of your father is to preserve his towering legacy of integrity, patriotism, and selfless service,” he said. Obasanjo urged the children to uphold their father’s principles and continue contributing to society, stressing that sustaining the values he represented would be the best way to honour his memory. He concluded by praying for divine comfort for the Cole family and the people of the Kalabari Kingdom as they mourned the late diplomat. “May the Almighty God grant the entire Cole family and the people of the Kalabari Kingdom the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss. May the noble soul of Ambassador Dele Cole find eternal rest,” he said. The post Dele Cole: Nigeria has lost one of its finest intellectuals — Obasanjo appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: APC PCC mobilizes all 10,000 support groups for Tinubu
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress APC Presidential Campaign Council PCC has gone all out to galvanize the party’s over 10,000 support groups as part of its grassroots mobilization strategies for the reelection of President Bola Tinubu. Consequently, the APC PCC said it has opened an online registration portal for registration and revalidation of support groups membership. Director of the Support Groups Mobilization Directorate of the 2027 APC-PCC and a former Deputy Governor of Nasarawa State, Hon. Silas Agara, announced the launch at the national secretariat of the Tinubu Support Group TSG on Sunday in Abuja. “Today, we are officially launching our online support group registration portal. The portal goes live today, 17 October 2026, and will remain open for five days, closing on 22 October 2026”, he said. He asked all groups and volunteer networks working for the President’s re-election to register within that window, “irrespective of whether they have previously registered with the party or another campaign structure.” According to him, the exercise “will enable us to verify participating groups, understand their geographical spread and organisational capacity, and establish a reliable database for effective coordination and nationwide engagement.” “I urge every group to take this exercise seriously. Our objective is to build a unified mobilisation structure that is organised, accountable, responsive and prepared for the demands of the campaign ahead,” Agara said. He described support groups as “a vital link between the party, the campaign organisation and the Nigerian people.” They “bring together communities, professional associations, interest groups and volunteers, helping to communicate the administration’s policies, explain its achievements and engage citizens on issues that matter to them,” he said. The directorate’s mandate, he added, is “to coordinate these groups, strengthen their organisational capacity and ensure that their activities complement the broader objectives of the APC presidential campaign.” Agara said the mobilisation drive is “anchored on the record of the Tinubu administration and its Renewed Hope Agenda.” “Over the past three years, President Tinubu has undertaken major economic and institutional reforms aimed at addressing longstanding structural challenges and placing Nigeria on a path towards sustainable growth,” he said. item.title: Kebbi Govt slams Malami over UNDP poverty report claim
item.description: The Kebbi Government has taken a swipe at the African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate, Abubakar Malami, SAN. The government faulted the ADC guber candidate’s use of a UNDP poverty report to criticise the APC-led administration in the state. The Commissioner for Information and Culture, Alhaji Yakubu Ahmed-BK, slammed Malami at a press briefing in Birnin Kebbi on Sunday. He alleged that the former Attorney-General of the Federation was exploiting the report to score political points ahead of the 2027 general elections, rather than offering constructive solutions to the state’s challenges. Ahmed-BK said one property reportedly ordered for confiscation in Birnin Kebbi in court proceedings involving the former minister could have funded more than 1,000 boreholes across the state. He said the government acknowledged the economic difficulties and security challenges confronting Nigeria, but accused Malami of politicising the hardship of the people for personal political advantage. Ahmed-BK expressed surprise that Malami, who served as Attorney-General of the Federation under the late President Muhammadu Buhari, was now using the poverty report to criticise the state government. According to him, the period covered by the UNDP report included the first term and part of the second term of the Buhari administration, during which Malami held a prominent position. He alleged that policies and actions during the previous administration contributed to the economic difficulties reflected in the report. Ahmed-BK also accused Malami of failing to adequately address insecurity in Kebbi during his time in the Federal Government, despite his influential position. He referred to reports published in June 2025 concerning alleged killings in Tadurga Ward of Zuru Emirate. “Malami’s reported figure of 200 deaths was subsequently disputed by local security agencies, government officials and the Zuru Emirate Council. “The subsequent clarifications reportedly put the death toll at fewer than 30. Malami just used the incident for political purposes,” he said. He accused the former minister of hypocrisy over the relationship between poverty and alleged corruption, citing court proceedings involving the confiscation of properties allegedly linked to him. Ahmed-BK argued that the allegations and court proceedings involving the former minister should be considered when assessing his criticism of the state’s poverty levels. item.dc:creator: Akinbayo Wahab
item.content:encoded: The Kebbi Government has taken a swipe at the African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate, Abubakar Malami, SAN. The government faulted the ADC guber candidate’s use of a UNDP poverty report to criticise the APC-led administration in the state. The Commissioner for Information and Culture, Alhaji Yakubu Ahmed-BK, slammed Malami at a press briefing in Birnin Kebbi on Sunday. He alleged that the former Attorney-General of the Federation was exploiting the report to score political points ahead of the 2027 general elections, rather than offering constructive solutions to the state’s challenges. Ahmed-BK said one property reportedly ordered for confiscation in Birnin Kebbi in court proceedings involving the former minister could have funded more than 1,000 boreholes across the state. He said the government acknowledged the economic difficulties and security challenges confronting Nigeria, but accused Malami of politicising the hardship of the people for personal political advantage. Ahmed-BK expressed surprise that Malami, who served as Attorney-General of the Federation under the late President Muhammadu Buhari, was now using the poverty report to criticise the state government. According to him, the period covered by the UNDP report included the first term and part of the second term of the Buhari administration, during which Malami held a prominent position. He alleged that policies and actions during the previous administration contributed to the economic difficulties reflected in the report. Ahmed-BK also accused Malami of failing to adequately address insecurity in Kebbi during his time in the Federal Government, despite his influential position. He referred to reports published in June 2025 concerning alleged killings in Tadurga Ward of Zuru Emirate. “Malami’s reported figure of 200 deaths was subsequently disputed by local security agencies, government officials and the Zuru Emirate Council. “The subsequent clarifications reportedly put the death toll at fewer than 30. Malami just used the incident for political purposes,” he said. He accused the former minister of hypocrisy over the relationship between poverty and alleged corruption, citing court proceedings involving the confiscation of properties allegedly linked to him. Ahmed-BK argued that the allegations and court proceedings involving the former minister should be considered when assessing his criticism of the state’s poverty levels. He also accused some former public office holders of seeking elective positions to shield themselves from accountability. On security, Ahmed-BK said the administration of Gov. Nasir Idris had taken several steps to strengthen security and support personnel combating banditry and other violent crimes across the state. He said the government had procured and donated hundreds of operational vehicles and thousands of motorcycles to security agencies. “These include the provision of welfare support to soldiers, police officers, personnel of the Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), hunters and vigilante groups. “The Governor has also visited communities affected by attacks to sympathise with victims, provide relief and assure residents of additional measures to improve security. “The administration has facilitated the establishment of forward operating bases and other military formations. “The formations include the 28 Armoured Brigade and Garrison in Birnin Kebbi, the 281 Tank Battalion in Yauri and the 381 Artillery Regiment in Kaoje,” he said. Ahmed-BK added that the state government was procuring additional armoured platforms to enhance security operations. On the government’s development agenda, the commissioner listed investments in health, education, road construction, economic empowerment, agricultural support, employment and workers’ welfare among the administration’s priorities. He said the government had distributed free fertilisers and other farming inputs, provided solar-powered and compressed natural gas (CNG)-powered pumps for wet- and dry-season farming, distributed food items and employed thousands of teachers. According to him, the administration had improved wages, paid scholarships and provided support for the registration and school fees of students studying within and outside Nigeria, as well as implemented cash-transfer interventions worth billions of Naira. Ahmed-BK described the administration’s road construction programme as a deliberate effort to addressing longstanding infrastructure deficits, particularly those affecting farmers and commercial activities. He cited the Koko-Zuru Road as an important agricultural and economic corridor, saying its poor condition over the years had affected the movement of farm produce and other goods. On solid minerals development, the commissioner said the state government had established a Ministry of Solid Minerals Development and a Solid Minerals Development Agency to regulate the sector, protect the interests of residents and attract investment. He said the government was in advanced discussions with local and foreign investors, adding that agreements had been signed and credit facilities advanced towards prospective investments. The commissioner acknowledged that the administration’s efforts had yet to fully address the poverty challenges facing the state. He argued that the scale of the problems required sustained interventions beyond the government’s first three years in office. Ahmed-BK called on the people of Kebbi to support the Idris administration, popularly known as Kauran Gwandu. “I urge the residents to give the administration another term, as continuity will enable ongoing projects and policies to deliver greater benefits to the state,” the commissioner pleaded. item.title: EPL: Leeds Frustrate Man United To Pile Pressure On Carrick
item.description: Manchester United ended a turbulent week with a frustrating 1-1 draw at Leeds on Sunday that does little to ease the pressure on beleaguered manager Michael Carrick. The Red Devils travelled to the home of their bitter rivals, desperate to find a spark after just two wins in nine games in all competitions this season. The sense of a growing crisis at the club was exacerbated in midweek by an outburst from defender Lisandro Martinez, who took aim at the United hierarchy after a 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. The Argentina centre-back said Carrick, in his first full season in charge at Old Trafford, had been left with an under-strength squad after an underwhelming summer transfer window. The United boss insisted on Friday that United had “moved on” from the incident, and Martinez was named in the starting line-up at Elland Road. Both teams were fully committed in a feisty start to the match in Leeds but there was little goalmouth action. The first effort on target came in the 26th minute when United goalkeeper Senne Lammens clawed away a Nico Elvedi header destined for the top corner after bouncing up off the turf. Bryan Mbeumo, playing as United’s target man, headed wastefully wide a minute later after a fine cross from Youri Tielemans and then shot tamely at Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford. But he finally broke the deadlock in the 35th minute when Tielemans again delivered a low ball from the right which Mbeumo guided into the bottom corner for his fourth Premier League goal of the season. Martinez went off at half-time as Morocco’s Noussair Mazraoui was brought into the action. Leeds started strongly after the break and were level in the 51st minute when Dominic Calvert-Lewin controlled the ball on his chest and finished at full stretch after Tarik Muharemovic got his head to the ball following a corner. Manchester United’s English head coach Michael Carrick (L) and Leeds United’s German head coach Daniel Farke (R) embrace on the final whistle in the English Premier League football match between Leeds United and Manchester United at Elland Road in Leeds, northern England on October 18, 2026. Photo: PAUL ELLIS / AFP The home team were now well on top, largely limiting Carrick’s team to counter-attacks. The United boss made attacking substitutions in the search for a winner, bringing on Mason Mount and Matheus Cunha, but neither team could force a winner. The point left 20-time English champions United in 13th place in the table with just one win in seven games while Leeds are seventh. item.title: Evanilson swivels his hips to seal Bournemouth win against 10-man Sunderland
item.description: Bournemouth’s, and Marco Rose’s, wait for a Premier League win is over. Sunderland, locked in the bottom three, are becoming this season’s object lesson in travelling too far, too fast. Once Kevin Danso was dismissed in the 17th minute for the denial of a goalscoring opportunity, Sunderland were sunk. If Evanilson was the match-winner with a goal, an assist and as the player Danso fouled, Régis Le Bris’s team were architects of their own downfall. “A bad day, a bad start,” said Sunderland’s manager. Sixth and seventh last season, both teams have struggled domestically while cruising in the Europa League but Sunderland’s troubles deepened. Continue reading...

item.title: Gómez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton’s 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal Palace
item.description: At last, Fabian Hürzeler has the scalp that matters most to all Brighton fans and in humiliating fashion. Diego Gómez’s breathtaking goal-of-the-season contender from the halfway line, à la David Beckham, was the highlight of another hugely impressive performance from the Premier League’s top scorers as they continued their flying start to the season. Not since a 4-1 thrashing here in February 2024 under Roberto De Zerbi had Brighton tasted victory against their arch rivals from up the A23 – a run of four matches. But having been handed the initiative by Jaydee Canvot’s own goal, a stunned Palace found themselves 3-0 down after 10 minutes. It got even worse for Pierre Sage after Brighton extended their lead through Gómez’s wonderstrike and Yasin Ayari, with Charalampos Kostoulas adding a fourth after half-time and the substitute Jack Hinshelwood’s late strike matching their record 5-0 win over Palace from 1956 in Division Three South. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘France Is Burning,’ ‘Shattered’ By Immigration, Says Trump
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Sunday blamed immigration for unrest during protests in France and urged the country to tighten its migration rules. “France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country,” Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform. “Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!” France was reeling Sunday from widespread damage during protests the day before that, which left a historic town hall torched and led to 1,800 arrests, piling pressure on President Emmanuel Macron six months before elections to replace him. This photograph shows a portion of the partially burnt facade of the Limoges city hall a day after riot and looting following nationwide protests against the “high cost of living” in Limoges on October 18, 2026. PASCAL LACHENAUD / AFP Trump’s post follows similar comments from Vice President JD Vance on Saturday. “Western liberals imported the third world into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion. They ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility. They were told it would lead to this, and they didn’t listen,” Vance wrote on X. “I pray that France, a beautiful country of amazing people, will stop this madness before more of its landmarks burn,” he added. Vance, seen as a potential presidential candidate in the 2028 election, also linked it to upcoming midterm races for congressional seats on November 3, where Republicans are not expected to perform well. AFP The post ‘France Is Burning,’ ‘Shattered’ By Immigration, Says Trump appeared first on Channels Television .

They were told it would lead to this, and they didn’t listen,” Vance wrote on X. “I pray that France, a beautiful country of amazing people, will stop this madness before more of its landmarks burn,” he added. Vance, seen as a potential presidential candidate in the 2028 election, also linked it to upcoming midterm races for congressional seats on November 3, where Republicans are not expected to perform well. AFP The post ‘France Is Burning,’ ‘Shattered’ By Immigration, Says Trump appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Lenovo’s fast, comfy SteamOS handheld is hundreds off
item.description: The Legion Go S with SteamOS is a pretty solid alternative to the $789 Steam Deck OLED. It runs identical software, but ships in a design with two-stage triggers, a bigger eight-inch IPS screen (1080p and up to 120Hz versus 800p and 90Hz in the Deck OLED), and it’s got double the RAM and storage (32GB and 1TB, respectively), not to mention a slightly faster processor in the Ryzen Z1 Extreme. At $999.99, its current discounted price at Best Buy , it’s worth considering if you’re deciding on a handheld. The Legion Go S is not as powerful as the $1,299.99 Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 that just launched, which has the Z2 Extreme and a OLED screen, but it’s no slouch, either. Lenovo Legion Go S with SteamOS (Z1 Extreme) Where to Buy: $1579.99 $999.99 at Best Buy This model launched with Windows 11 and the Ryzen Z2 Go. Despite being a newer chip, it’s less powerful than the Z1 Extreme in the discounted model. SteamOS and the faster internals within this configuration will provide a better experience. Check out my colleague Sean Hollister’s review of multiple configs of the Go S, and see how it stacks up in his benchmarks.

item.title: Lagos Airport Rail Project Financing Talks At Advanced Stage – FAAN MD
item.description: Discussions on financing the planned extension of the Lagos Mass Transit Red Line to Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA) are at an advanced stage, the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Olubunmi Onabanjo-Kuku, has said. The project, planned by the Federal Government in collaboration with FAAN, will link the airport’s three terminals to the Red Line as part of the wider MMIA modernisation project. Speaking as a keynote panellist at the World Aviation Festival in Lisbon, Portugal, Kuku said efforts were ongoing to finalise the project’s financing structure. “We are actually working on completing the financing of the capital structure for that project,” she said. Kuku explained that the rail link would improve access between the city and the airport, with five stops within the airport serving its terminals and cargo facilities. “It allows us to connect the city very quickly to the airport with five stops within our airport. It connects our terminals and links our cargo terminals to the last stop,” she said, adding that the project would involve collaboration between the Lagos State and Federal Governments. FAAN MD Olubunmi Onabanjo-Kuku speaking as a keynote panellist at the World Aviation Festival in Lisbon, Portugal. On the ongoing upgrade of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Kuku said the project would make the facility more efficient and passenger-friendly through improved infrastructure and modern technology. She noted that the Lagos airport accounts for 68 per cent of Nigeria’s air traffic, while Abuja and Kano are among the country’s other major aviation hubs. According to her, the three airports account for 80 per cent of passenger traffic, making it necessary for FAAN to balance investment in the busiest facilities with the needs of other airports under its management. Kuku said safety remained a major consideration in determining the agency’s investment priorities, with much of its spending focused on airside infrastructure and the rehabilitation of major airports. “In the last three years, we focused on rehabilitating our major airports and the primary international airports,” she said. She added that runway rehabilitation, including the resurfacing of runway extensions where possible, and the installation of improved airfield lighting systems were among the ongoing works at two of the country’s six international airports. On Lagos specifically, Kuku said Terminal 1 was undergoing a comprehensive overhaul but would not be expanded. Instead, the work would focus on improving the terminal’s layout, including immigration and customs facilities, increasing efficiency at service counters and introducing modern technology to make the passenger experience smoother. “We’re changing the layout with immigration and customs, the number of counters that you have, making it a lot more passenger-friendly, ensuring that we have modernised technology and infrastructure that makes travel easier for p

item.title: ‘Like We Had A War’: France Counts Cost Of Violent Protests
item.description: France was reeling on Sunday from widespread damage caused by violent protests the day before that saw 1,800 people arrested, a historic town hall torched and widespread looting. “It’s like we had a war,” a 78-year-old resident in central Paris, Mehmet Ozeden, told AFP amid burnt street barricades from the protests. This photograph shows the partially burnt facade of the Limoges city hall a day after riot and looting following nationwide protests against the “high cost of living” in Limoges on October 18, 2026. (Photo by PASCAL LACHENAUD / AFP) | PASCAL LACHENAUD / AFP The convulsion raised the stakes for President Emmanuel Macron, who is in his final months in power before elections to replace him in six months’ time. It followed weeks of student protests that had also turned violent at times. Macron was to address the nation Sunday evening at 1800 GMT, his office said, after meeting key ministers. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 1,800 people were arrested over the protests and looting, with investigations under way “to identify the perpetrators of these acts so they can be brought to justice”. Torched cars, smashed shopfronts and burnt debris scarred numerous streets in Paris, where officials said 557 people were in custody after a “record” number of arrests. The capital experienced “a level of violence that we have never, I believe, seen before”, said Paris deputy mayor Lamia El Aaraje. People take part in a demonstration part of a nationwide day of actions called by high school students’ unions, who for days have been demanding better learning conditions in protests punctuated by violent confrontations, in Marseille on October 8, 2026. Photo by MIGUEL MEDINA / AFP Hundreds of shops were looted in Paris and other cities, including Marseille, Bordeaux, Nice and Strasbourg, during the protests over the cost of living. One person died during the main march in Paris, but officials said it was health-related and not linked to the protest violence. Around 1,500 businesses were damaged, causing losses estimated in the hundreds of millions of euros, according to the Retail and Trade Federation. One Paris resident, Anita Gras, out for a jog between the debris, said she saw young men loot a sports shoe retailer. “They stayed until 1:00 am; we were afraid they were going to throw things at us,” she said. “It’s appalling, terrifying — groups of young people came here yesterday (Saturday), looting, smashing everything, with total impunity,” said another resident, 57-year-old Cecile Rogue, surveying a pile of charred bicycles. ‘Wild Horde’ The city of Limoges lost its 19th-century town hall to a fire. The local prefect, Maurice Barate, told news channel LCI it had been deliberately set by “a wild horde” and was only brought under control early Sunday. item.dc:creator: Aramide Folorunsho
item.content:encoded: France was reeling on Sunday from widespread damage caused by violent protests the day before that saw 1,800 people arrested, a historic town hall torched and widespread looting. “It’s like we had a war,” a 78-year-old resident in central Paris, Mehmet Ozeden, told AFP amid burnt street barricades from the protests. This photograph shows the partially burnt facade of the Limoges city hall a day after riot and looting following nationwide protests against the “high cost of living” in Limoges on October 18, 2026. (Photo by PASCAL LACHENAUD / AFP) | PASCAL LACHENAUD / AFP The convulsion raised the stakes for President Emmanuel Macron, who is in his final months in power before elections to replace him in six months’ time. It followed weeks of student protests that had also turned violent at times. Macron was to address the nation Sunday evening at 1800 GMT, his office said, after meeting key ministers. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 1,800 people were arrested over the protests and looting, with investigations under way “to identify the perpetrators of these acts so they can be brought to justice”. Torched cars, smashed shopfronts and burnt debris scarred numerous streets in Paris, where officials said 557 people were in custody after a “record” number of arrests. The capital experienced “a level of violence that we have never, I believe, seen before”, said Paris deputy mayor Lamia El Aaraje. People take part in a demonstration part of a nationwide day of actions called by high school students’ unions, who for days have been demanding better learning conditions in protests punctuated by violent confrontations, in Marseille on October 8, 2026. Photo by MIGUEL MEDINA / AFP Hundreds of shops were looted in Paris and other cities, including Marseille, Bordeaux, Nice and Strasbourg, during the protests over the cost of living. One person died during the main march in Paris, but officials said it was health-related and not linked to the protest violence. Around 1,500 businesses were damaged, causing losses estimated in the hundreds of millions of euros, according to the Retail and Trade Federation. One Paris resident, Anita Gras, out for a jog between the debris, said she saw young men loot a sports shoe retailer. “They stayed until 1:00 am; we were afraid they were going to throw things at us,” she said. “It’s appalling, terrifying — groups of young people came here yesterday (Saturday), looting, smashing everything, with total impunity,” said another resident, 57-year-old Cecile Rogue, surveying a pile of charred bicycles. ‘Wild Horde’ The city of Limoges lost its 19th-century town hall to a fire. The local prefect, Maurice Barate, told news channel LCI it had been deliberately set by “a wild horde” and was only brought under control early Sunday. The mayor of Lyon, Gregory Doucet, said, “The chaos that reigned in the city for several hours was abominable.” A tourist office in the centre of Lyon was set ablaze during the protests, which saw multiple clashes and looting. Political recriminations have followed, with the government and far-right leader Marine Le Pen blaming ultra-left groups, while far-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon accused authorities of inflaming tensions. Paris’s Socialist deputy mayor El Aaraje accused Le Pen’s party of “acting like a pyromaniac firefighter”, using the protests to further her presidential ambitions. US Vice President JD Vance also waded in, implying on X that the unrest was because France had “imported the third world”. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu was to chair a crisis meeting of ministers at 0800 GMT on Monday, his office said. They were to look at the insurance and help impacted shops as well as prosecute perpetrators of the violence. Half A Million Demonstrators A protester throws a smoke flare towards French gendarmes during a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, in Bordeaux, southwestern France, on October 17, 2026 as part of a nationwide call for mobilisation bringing together various groups expressing their anger: former “Yellow Vest”, secondary school and university students, climate activists and even farmers. Photo by CHRISTOPHE ARCHAMBAULT / AFP In Paris, startled tourists were seen running with suitcases along streets filled with tear gas and protesters on Saturday. A Danish tourist, Soren Petersen, said it was “sad” to see damage to Paris buildings. “It is not a protest; it’s far beyond a normal protest,” he told AFP. An American tourist, Jill Burns, said, “We were scared.” Around 500 police, firefighters and paramedics were hurt in the protests, the interior minister said. The violence took place on the sidelines of nationwide protests that the interior ministry said were attended by 550,000 people. The CGT union said 800,000 people participated. A 17-year-old boy had his right hand blown off by a crowd-control grenade in the southern city of Saint-Etienne. Analyst Mujtaba Rahman of the Eurasia Group think tank said on X that most of the demonstrations Saturday were peaceful, and “the violence came from a fringe of the ultra left” with looting “by opportunistic gangs from the poor suburbs”. “All good news for Marine Le Pen,” he said. France’s Yellow Vest movement, which staged street protests eight years ago against Macron’s government over planned fuel-tax hikes, had called Saturday’s “yellow and youth” demonstrations. The principal grievance was the cost of living, pushed up in part by the war in the Middle East, which has helped send inflation soaring in Europe as elsewhere.
